articleTitle: Employee Retention and Layoff Prediction Using Machine Learning: A Comparative Study of XGBoost and KMeans
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Employee retention and layoff predictions are now one of the big challenges that organizations in different sectors face, especially in highly turning-over industries or those whose labor fluctuation varies according to seasonal trends. The present paper applies the study of machine learning to predict retention and layoff likelihood among the employees by focusing on the performance of two models: XGBoost, a classification model, and KMeans, a clustering model. Using employee tenure, performance ratings, and engagement scores variables, we compare each of the models in their accuracy, interpretability, and forecasting capability at predicting whether an employee is likely to remain or face the threat of layoff. XGBoost highly excels with regard to binary prediction while KMeans is very revealing about what characterization different groups of employees attract. It was able to compare these approaches and then concluded that XGBoost is an enhanced model regarding accurate layoff prediction where it directly gives simple “yes” or “no” outcomes that help in practical HR planning. These results strengthen the potential of machine learning as a material for predictive workforce management, yielding actionable insights for human resource departments and re- asserting strategic workforce planning.

articleTitle: Enhanced Performance of Two- Stage Operational Amplifier Through Dual-Gate CNTFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: An optimistic option for upcoming electronic devices with small potential power, small-voltage mixed circuit applications are the carbon nanotube field-effect transistor (CNTFET). A small-voltage, small-power, two-stage operational amplifier (OP AMP) on cutting-edge automation CNTFET was introduced in this paper. The suggested Dual gate-CNTFET (DG-CNTFET) operational amplifier (OP AMP) performance characteristics are examined and contrasted with those of the current CMOS sub-32nm technology. HSPICE and cadence software is used to simulate a circuit at an input supply voltage of 2V to determine the performance parameters of the operational amplifier [2]. Based on simulation results, the suggested DG-CNTFET OP AMP circuit achieves more DC gain of over 40dB, more band width gains up to 196MHz, phase margin of 45degrees, output swing of 2V, settling time of O.85ns, CMRR of 53.54dB, PSRR of 53.54dB, and small static power usage of 10W. The outputs indicate the carbon nanotube (CNT) operational amplifier has promise for small power, more speed implementation in mixed-signal and analog nano electronic circuits

articleTitle: Land Cover Classification using Satellite Imagery and Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Remote sensing has evidenced itself as a more efficient source of quantitative data than ground based surveys in terms of time and space. Remote sensing is crucial in the collection of data for many aspects of life or areas, such as political, economic, Urban Planning, Agriculture, Forestry, Barren, and even scientific. Land cover data is useful with regard to planning and decision making processes in urban areas and it has several solutions in terms of mapping and monitoring of the urban areas. A satellite image categorization based mainly on urban planning, land-use mapping, and environmental monitoring is used. Within this context, this study explores the possibility of bringing reinforcement learning in conjunction with pertinent point-matching techniques into the analysis of Landsat satellite picture classification via the Google Earth Engine (GEE). As opposed to the classic application of traditional supervised and unsupervised model in the process of satellite image classification, the RL presents a dynamic approach, strongly dependent on feedback for possible improvement over time in classification accuracy. This is further enhanced by key point matching, which makes it possible to identify important characteristics in many temporal pictures, recognize objects, and detect changes more robustly. In our discussion of a unique framework, we highlight the potential advantages of feature correspondence and adaptive categorization in complicated satellite data by integrating RL and key point matching with GEE's cloud based infrastructure. Results from experiments show how well this hybrid model works to increase classification accuracy.

articleTitle: High-Performance Digital Circuit Architectures for Accelerated Number Theoretic Transform Computation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This research paper aims to improve the applications that need fast polynomial multiplication, particularly errors-correcting codes and encryption, where the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) is an essential tool. High-performance digital circuit topologies that accelerate modular arithmetic operations, including modular multiplication, subtraction, and addition, are proposed in this work to increase the efficiency of NTT computation. The architecture uses parallel processing and pipeline techniques to greatly increase performance. The implementation of optimization techniques can also be part of the resource-sharing systems, bit-reversal elimination, and efficient butterfly unit design, which also reduces latency and area overhead. The recommended design is developed and evaluated using a digital simulation framework, yielding a significant improvement in throughput and energy efficiency compared to existing systems. The experiments that demonstrate the design are scaled for input sizes and are appropriate for real-time cryptography systems. This work replicates the groundwork for the usage of NTT computation in the future with safe and efficient computing systems by moving into how algorithmic developments and hardware optimizations can be work together to provide high-speed NTT computation.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in Solar Panels Using Time Series Analysis and CNN
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: An automated and efficient way to check solar panels for flaws has become essential as the demand for solar energy systems grows worldwide. Our project takes a double approach to meeting this demand. First, we apply the convolutional neural network (CNN) VGG16 for image-based solar power panel fault identification. This technique uses transfer learning to detect surface irregularities with accuracy. Second, we use the ARIMA model to forecast possible problems and analyse power generation data to identify performance trends we demonstrate the application of ARIMA for time series analysis in solar power plants. The goal is to detect underperforming and faulty solar panels by analysing 30 days of power generation data. ARIMA is employed to forecast the expected power output of each panel, and deviations from the forecast indicate potential issues. This method ensures timely detection of malfunctioning panels, leading to improved maintenance efficiency and increased energy yield.

articleTitle: Obstacle Detection on Autonomous Driving Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Self-driving cars, also known as autonomous vehicles are capable of supplanting automobiles driven by humans. In situations that humans find difficult, autonomous vehicles are able to examine their surroundings and ease through roadways. Many people might soon turn very dependent on AVs and overconfident that there won't be any failures owing to this. This has resulted in AVs having both affirmative as well as bad hands on the society. A combination of hardware, software, people, and their interactions, AVs are X-ware systems. There are still a lot of unanswered questions regarding AVs despite the abundance of research on the subject. Communication with pedestrians and other cars on the road is one of the biggest problems facing AVs. There must be an interaction between AVs and other transport users if autonomous cars have to replace human- driven vehicles. Few previous studies have examined the role of humans in the present shift to a society where self-driving cars are the norm, whereas the majority have focused on software errors. Three perspectives are examined in this paper: I that of the AV's driver and passenger; II that of pedestrians; and III that of the AV's interactions with other users of the transportation network. We also talk about relevant behavioral research.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a 10 GHz Microstrip Patch Antenna with Coaxial Probe Feed for 50 Ω Characteristic Impedance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a 10 GHz microstrip patch antenna having a characteristic impedance of 50 Ω and coaxial probe feed. The proposed antenna boasts a physical dimension of 10 ×9 ×0.32 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>and excellent efficiency and compactness. The key performance parameters include the gain, VSWR and return loss. The 462 MHz bandwidth of the antenna establishes its suitability for high-frequency applications. The impedance between the feed line is extremely well matched by this design, with an impedance of 50.56 Ω The axial ratio of 3.359 also manifests moderate circular polarisation abilities. Such findings prove the coaxial probe-fed design's effectiveness, and it is on the forefront for use in the radar and wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Adaptive MobileNet Framework for Human Signature Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In an era of more digital interaction, authenticating persons through handwritten signatures is crucial. This study presents an Adaptive MobileNet Framework for accurate hand-written signature recognition, integrating MobileNet's lightweight architecture with adaptive methodologies to enhance performance. The framework improves feature extraction and utilizes transfer learning to increase accuracy across various signature styles. We rigorously assess the model's efficacy utilizing an extensive dataset of authentic signatures from various sources. Experimental findings indicate that the Adaptive MobileNet Framework far surpasses conventional recognition systems, with an accuracy of 91.5%, precision of 90.8%, and recall of 91.2%. The framework is optimized for optimal computing resource utilization, making it appropriate for mobile and embedded devices, hence facilitating real-time signature verification.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Detection Using Guided Filtering and SVM Classifier
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: One of the major reasons for a large number of deaths around the world is cancer. Among various kinds of cancers, lung cancer is responsible for a large number of deaths. Therefore, early detection of it is very necessary to save patients life, and provide required treatment. The reliance of conventional diagnostic techniques on radiologist expertise can cause errors and delays in diagnosis, and both CT scans and X-rays are often hindered. This research article proposes an automated method based on guided filtering for image enhancement, and a SVM classifier for lung cancer detection. These applications employ guided filtering to reduce noise and improve the edge details of lung CT images in order to get improved feature extraction. The processed enhanced images train an SVM classifier that achieves good separation of cancerous and non-cancerous regions using extracted features. Results of experiments show the proposed method achieves high classification accuracy in which its sensitivity and specificity are superior to standard methods. This method can also be used to clearly automatically and reliably detect lung cancer so that healthcare professionals would be able to early diagnose and improve patient's outcome.

articleTitle: Amalgamation of Cryptography and Steganography for Securing the Healthcare Data Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Healthcare data breaches remain a prominent threat to patients’ privacy as well as an institution's integrity. Traditional forms of encryption no longer suffice as cyberattacks develop into sophisticated attacks, and this article explores the concept of synergizing cryptographic algorithms with steganographic methods to improve health care data safety. Surveyed 47 hospitals that have adopted this hybrid approach based on AES-256 encryption and used LSB steganography in the medical imaging file. Results have been shown to achieve a 94% reduction in successful unauthorized access attempts when compared to single-layer security systems. Data retrieval efficiency is also preserved with only a 2.3% increase in processing overhead. Dual-layer protection has also been effective in man-in-the-middle attacks since no successful breach was detected within six months of testing. This research established that the fusion of cryptography and steganography would provide an appropriate security framework for healthcare data that would increase security without significant overhead on system performance. These results are important in ensuring that the infrastructure of health organizations is strengthened as much as possible while operational efficiency is also achieved.

articleTitle: Optimized Smart Wearable Device for Man Overboard Detection and Identification System in Marine
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Maritime safety is a persistent problem, particularly for ferry, yacht, and commercial ship crew. Man Overboard (MOB) detection generally relies on human vision and thus has a relatively slower response. This paper introduces a new IoT-based wearable system that is responsible for real-time MOB condition monitoring and instant alerting of others. The system employs an array of sensors: MAX30102 for monitoring heart rate and SpO2 level, MPU6050 for detecting movement and falls, and a pH sensor for detecting water submersion. When hazardous levels are detected, the NEO-6M GPS module activates to get the exact location and sends an emergency message through a Wi-Fi module to pre-programmed responders or onboard systems. This solution optimizes response time, reducing the risk of missed MOB events and improving survival chances. The device is versatile for use across maritime industries, including logistics, passenger transport, naval operations, and recreational boating.

articleTitle: UPI-Based E-Vehicle Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and electric vehicle (EV) charging station integration is a major step towards improving the usability and effectiveness of the infrastructure supporting EVs. The National Payments Corporation of India created the novel UPI payment system, which enables quick and easy financial transactions using mobile devices. Users gain from a simplified payment procedure that eliminates the need for conventional, frequently laborious payment methods like cash or credit/debit cards by integrating UPI into EV charging stations. Creating a reliable payment gateway that communicates with the hardware and software of the E- V charging station is the first step in this integration. Through a mobile app, the UPI-based system enables a speedy transaction when a user starts a charging session.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Strategies for Nifty50 Index Trading Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The dynamic nature of financial markets, especially Nifty50 trading, requires advanced predictive models for effective decision-making and risk management. Recent advancements in machine learning have led to robust models for handling financial data complexities and market volatility. This review explores a number of machine learning algorithms ensemble methods, and deep learning models. Key stages such as data pre-processing, feature selection, and model training are analyzed, with a focus on integrating the India VIX index and financial indicators to improve accuracy. Comparative performance analysis using metrics like accuracy, sensitivity, MAPE, RMSE, and F1-Score is presented. The paper concludes with insights on how these advancements can enhance prediction precision, risk management, and trading outcomes.

articleTitle: From Image to Recipe: Transfer Learning for Identifying Food Ingredients
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Although there has been a lot of advancement in the use of AI in food technology, ingredient detection is still difficult since food textures and looks vary so much. A potential remedy is transfer learning, which leverages prior knowledge to improve performance on particular datasets by customizing pre-trained models for novel tasks. The use of deep learning to analyses food images has attracted a lot of attention lately, especially because of its potential to transform the culinary and nutritional sciences. The effectiveness of transfer learning models, such as Xception, ResNet50, and EfficientNet, for detecting components from food photos is investigated in this work. The background research emphasizes the developments in convolutional neural networks and their efficacy in a range of picture classification tasks, highlighting the necessity of precise ingredient identification systems in applications such as recipe suggestion and nutritional monitoring. Using a carefully chosen collection of food photos labelled with matching ingredients, the process comprises optimizing pre-trained models. The design of each model is customized to address the multi-label categorization issue that arises during the identification of ingredients. Techniques like data augmentation are used to train and evaluate the models. The findings show that ResNet50 with 92% and Xception with an accuracy of 85% obtain the maximum accuracy. EffectiveNet variations also exhibit good performance, with top-1 accuracy reaching 70%, especially eff6 and eff7. In summary, the research finds that transfer learning models ResNet50 and Xception in particular are very successful in identifying ingredients, opening the door to reliable, practical uses in nutrition analysis and food technology.

articleTitle: FlaskOCR: Building a Framework for Text Extraction From Image
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Text recognition has become a favored topic in the field of computer vision. Research in this field has great potential to benefit many domains worldwide. Examples include text visualization, document classification, and license plate identification. Many researchers working on this topic have developed methods for identifying text using Optical Character Recognition (OCR). OCR serves as a diagnostic tool in fields such as machine vision, pattern recognition, and machine intelligence. Handwriting recognition, a key area of OCR, is widely used to evaluate a computer's ability to translate human-written text into digital form. This can be achieved through scanning handwritten text or typing directly into a designated input field. Although OCR has nearly solved the problem of text recognition for Latin characters, challenges remain for non-Latin scripts. Recognizing non-Latin text is particularly difficult because its appearance often differs significantly in contour and layout compared to the Latin text. This study aims to compile a comprehensive collection of OCR databases. A total of 5,900 characters were prepared and processed in various ways using Tesseract OCR tools. The FlaskOCR project was developed to create an OCR system capable of recognizing both online and offline handwriting.

articleTitle: Beamforming for 6G ISAC Systems:A Comparative Study of Reconfigurable Holographic Surfaces and Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) is emerging as a pivotal technology for next-generation 6G networks, enabling simultaneous wireless communication and environmental sensing. This paper investigates the integration of Reconfigurable Holographic Surfaces (RHS) and phased array antennas within ISAC systems to enhance both functionalities. The proposed system leverages RHS to dynamically manipulate electromagnetic wave reflections, improving communication coverage and sensing accuracy. A comparative analysis is conducted between RHS and phased array beamforming models, emphasizing advancements in beamforming precision, interference suppression, and spectral efficiency. Numerical simulations demonstrate that RHS-based ISAC significantly outperforms conventional phased arrays, achieving up to an 8 dB Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) enhancement in high-element configurations. The findings highlight RHS as a scalable and efficient technology for ISAC applications, underscoring its potential for future wireless communication systems. Further research is necessary to optimize hardware implementations and develop advanced beamforming algorithms for real-world deployment.

articleTitle: ProStock: Professional Stock Market Navigation and Analysis Suite
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This article presents ProStock: Professional Stock Market Navigation and Analysis Suite is a comprehensive platform designed for traders, investors, and financial analysts, offering advanced tools for real-time stock market analysis and portfolio management. The system leverages data from multiple financial markets, providing detailed insights through cutting-edge analytics, technical indicators, and AI-driven predictive models. With an intuitive interface, users can easily monitor stock performance, track market trends, and receive personalized alerts based on custom trading strategies, ensuring informed decision-making in fastpaced trading environments. ProStock integrates artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance market predictions and stock valuations. The platform's algorithms analyze vast datasets, identifying patterns and anomalies to forecast stock price movements, volatility, and potential risks. Additionally, its NLP-based news sentiment analysis feature processes real-time news, social media feeds, and financial reports, helping users understand market sentiment and its potential impact on stock performance. Designed with usercentricity in mind, ProStock allows for customization, enabling users to create personalized dashboards and charts. Whether for day traders seeking minute-by-minute updates or longterm investors monitoring portfolio growth, ProStock offers flexible options for both novice and expert users. The platform also supports multi-device synchronization, making it accessible on desktop and mobile devices, ensuring seamless access to stock market data anywhere, anytime.

articleTitle: A Software-Driven License Plate Recognition System for VIP Parking Utilizing HRNet and LPRNet with OpenCV and OCR
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The fully software-driven License Plate Recognition (LPR) system aimed at managing VIP parking access, leveraging state-of-the-art computer vision techniques. The system employs HRNet for accurate real-time detection of license plates and utilizes LPRNet for efficient alphanumeric extraction of characters. By integrating OpenCV and Tesseract Optical Character Recognition (OCR), the solution eliminates the need for specialized hardware, allowing seamless integration with standard camera systems. Advanced image preprocessing methods, including adaptive thresholding, morphological transformations, and noise reduction, significantly enhance text recognition accuracy across varying environmental conditions such as lighting, occlusion, and motion blur. Furthermore, the system incorporates machine learning techniques for validating VIP access by matching the extracted license plate characters with an established database. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the system's high precision, with a recognition accuracy exceeding 96% under controlled conditions and 85% in more challenging environments, such as low-light scenarios. This scalable and cost-efficient solution paves the way for broader applications in automated access control, intelligent transportation systems, and urban mobility infrastructure, demonstrating potential for large-scale deployment in smart city environments. The proposed system reduces operational costs by eliminating the need for specialized hardware and offers easy scalability for integration with existing infrastructure. Future enhancements include the continued development of deep learning-based detection algorithms, particularly leveraging HRNet and LPRNet, positioning this solution as a key component in smart parking and automated vehicle management systems.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Crop Health: CNN and XGBoost for Accurate Disease Detection in Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Smart agriculture is revolutionizing conventional agricultural methods by utilizing new technologies for improved crop monitoring and health management. This research introduces a hybrid model that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with XGBoost for precise detection of root rot disease, with the objective of transforming crop health management. The CNN model is employed for automated feature extraction from leaf photos, identifying complex patterns linked to root rot illness. The features are subsequently input into the XGBoost classifier, recognized for its efficiency and accuracy, to deliver reliable illness prediction. Comprehensive experiments utilizing the Coconut Tree Disease Dataset revealed that the proposed hybrid method attained a remarkable average accuracy of 91%, exceeding the performance of conventional machine learning (ML) models, including CNN, MLP, SVM, and XGBoost, which achieved accuracies of 86%,81%, 83%, and 88%, respectively. The suggested framework establishes a basis for a scalable and intelligent plant health monitoring system, promoting sustainable and smart agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Adaptive Water Resource Allocation in Smart Agriculture using Time-Varying Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Effective allocation of water resources is essential for sustainable agriculture, particularly in smart farming contexts where improving resource utilization can improve crop output and resilience. This paper presents an adaptive approach for water resource allocation that employs Time-Varying Bayesian Networks (TVBNs) to dynamically model water needs based on real-time environmental and crop-specific data. Our methodology dynamically modifies water distribution by integrating time-sensitive variables and probabilistic analyses, accounting for seasonal variations, soil moisture content, and stages of crop development. Experimental findings indicate that the suggested TVBN model attains a mean accuracy of 92.5% in forecasting water requirements, markedly enhancing water consumption efficiency and minimizing waste. These findings provide a scalable approach for adaptive irrigation in intelligent agricultural systems, underscoring the potential of TVBNs to improve sustainable farming methods.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Legal Workflows: Advanced AI Techniques for Document Summarization, Legal Translation, and Conversational Assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of legal documents necessitate more efficient processing and analysis. we propose an AI-driven approach to streamline legal services by integrating advanced natural language processing (NLP) models for summarization, translation, and conversational assistance. We utilize the allenai/led-base-16384 model for summarization of extensive legal documents, Facebook M2M-100 for multi-lingual translation, and mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 for legal conversational AI. The proposed system enhances legal services by providing quick, accurate summaries, translations, and AI-driven legal advice, thereby improving accessibility and reducing time and cost for legal professionals. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the system on various legal documents, highlighting its potential to revolutionize legal workflows.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model for Predicting Tensile Strength of Aluminium Alloy 5083
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Aluminium alloy 5083 is widely employed in various industries owing to its exceptional corrosion resistance, weld-ability, and high strength-to-weight ratio. Accurate prediction of its tensile strength is crucial for improving manufacturing processes and guaranteeing material performance under diverse conditions. This study presents a machine learning (ML) model designed to predict the tensile strength of aluminium alloy 5083, utilizing experimental data as input elements, such as material composition, processing parameters, and environmental variables. Various ML techniques, including Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gradient Boosting (GB), were evaluated to identify the most efficient predictor. Methods for feature selection were utilized to enhance model performance and clarity. The proposed model exhibited enhanced predictive accuracy, attaining a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.33 MPa, a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 2.83 MPa, and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> score of 0.94, surpassing traditional regression models. This technology offers a dependable and efficient instrument for manufacturers to forecast and control the tensile strength of aluminium alloy 5083, thereby lowering costs and enhancing product quality.

articleTitle: Efficient Techniques for Differential Privacy in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Privacy leakage in deep learning models trained on sensitive data is a growing concern, particularly in preventing data regurgitation and membership inference attacks. Differential Privacy (DP) provides a formal framework to mitigate these risks, yet conventional approaches like Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) suffer from substantial computational overhead and performance degradation. This work introduces novel techniques to improve DP training efficiency, particularly for large pretrained models such as Transformers. Empirical results show that strategic optimizations can significantly enhance the privacy-utility trade-off while reducing the high memory demands associated with DP implementations. Furthermore, theoretical analyses challenge existing assumptions, demonstrating dimension-independent performance bounds in specific optimization scenarios. These findings contribute to advancing differentially private machine learning, with practical implications in industry, including integration into Microsoft's privacy-preserving initiatives. The research underscores the importance of optimizing DP techniques for real-world applications and provides a foundation for further innovations in safeguarding sensitive data.

articleTitle: Exploring Vision-Based Models Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This study aims to integrate Kolmogorov Arnold Networks with vision based deep learning tasks. We hope to provide a comparative analysis between vision based deep learning models implemented using traditional methods and using Kolmogorov Arnold Networks. We have attempted this task specifically for two models: Image Classification and Image captioning. Our goal is to create these alternative KAN models and determine if they stand as a viable alternative. Our findings shed light on the scenarios where KAN's are applicable and adds to their capability in processing image data compared to pre-existing models further highlighting their value as an addition to the deep learning toolkit.

articleTitle: Robust Solar Powered DC Drive for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This paper explains the working of robust solar powered DC Drive for Electric Vehicle (EV) applications. Solar powered EVs are highly unstable; the stability and reliability is obtained with the help of DSMFC. The DC drive is powered by solar and the maximum power is obtained by MPPT technique. The MPPT algorithm adjusts the gate pulse of the Boost Converter and the output of the same is given to the DC Bus. The battery controller takes input from the DC bus and controls the battery. The EV takes power from the DC bus; the voltage given to the DC drive is adjusted by controlling the gate pulse of the chopper by DSMFC. The robustness of the drive is proved by adjusting the reference speed of the drive, introducing shading effect and varying irradiation of the PV array.

articleTitle: Predicting Breast Cancer by Analysing Wisconsin Dataset Through Machine Learning Algorithms Using Orange Tool
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Breast cancer is still a major global health issue, and early detection is important for better patient outcomes. This research discusses the use of machine learning algorithms for predicting breast cancer through the Orange data mining software. We utilized a comprehensive dataset containing various breast cancer features to develop and evaluate multiple machine learning models. The Orange tool facilitated data preprocessing, feature selection, model training, and performance evaluation. Our analysis compared the efficacy of several algorithms, in-cluding random forests, support vector machines, KNN, Gradient Boosting and neural networks. The study highlights the potential of orange tool for machine learning in enhancing breast cancer detection and diagnosis, potentially aiding healthcare profession-als in making more informed decisions. Furthermore, the user-friendly interface of the Orange tool showcases its utility in medical research and potential for wider adoption in clinical settings. For this paper, we consulted the Wisconsin dataset. The findings reveal that SVM models, particularly those utilizing ensemble methods like bagging and boosting with RBF kernels, significantly outperform traditional classifiers in both small and large datasets. In contrast, while Neural Networks demonstrated competitive accuracy, they often faced challenges related to overfitting and computational demands. Feature selection techniques were identified as crucial for enhancing model performance, allowing for more efficient training processes.

articleTitle: PM4GenAI: A Scriptable Parametric Modeling Interface for Generative AI-Driven Architecture Design Using PM4VR
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The integration of generative AI into computational design has led to groundbreaking advancements in various fields, including architecture, engineering, and industrial design. However, leveraging the full potential of AI-driven design requires intuitive tools that combine the power of algorithmic scripting with the flexibility of machine learning. This paper introduces PM4GenAI, a scriptable parametric modeling interface designed to bridge this gap, enabling seamless interaction between parametric design workflows and generative AI algorithms. Built on the PM4VR platform, PM4GenAI empowers designers to leverage AI's generative capabilities while maintaining control over the design process through parametric modeling. We clarify the PM4GenAI's framework and demonstrate its potential to foster innovative design solutions through experiment results.

articleTitle: Thermal Behavior and Bandgap Tuning of AlGaN Alloys for High Electron Mobility Transistors
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The temperature-dependent energy bandgap <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{E}_{\boldsymbol{g}}(\boldsymbol{T}))$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Al}_{\boldsymbol{x}}\boldsymbol{Ga}_{\boldsymbol{1-x}}\boldsymbol{N}$</tex> for High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMT) is modeled using the Manogé model, which incorporates electron-phonon interactions via the average phonon energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\langle\hbar \omega\rangle)}$</tex> and a dimensionless coupling constant (S). This study investigates the effects of varying aluminum composition (x) in AlGaN from 0.1 to 0.9, different coupling constants (S=1.5,2.0,2.5), Electron-Phonon Energy and temperatures ranging from 0 K to 600 K. The bowing parameter b=0.53 is fixed to account for the compositional nonlinearity in the bandgap energy. Results reveal that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}_{\boldsymbol{g}}(\boldsymbol{T})$</tex> decreases with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon interactions, and this effect becomes more pronounced at higher values of S. The analysis also explores the rate of change of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}_{\boldsymbol{g}}(\boldsymbol{T})$</tex>, providing insights into the thermal behavior of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{Al}_{\boldsymbol{x}}\boldsymbol{Ga}_{\boldsymbol{1-x}}\boldsymbol{N}$</tex>. This study highlights the critical role of material composition and thermal effects in the design of AlGaN-based HEMT for optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Super Resolution Techniques on Infrared Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This paper provides deep learning techniques for Super Resolution (SR) of a single infrared image. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly enhanced SR techniques. Infrared (IR) image super-resolution holds great potential for improving applications like object detection and classification by recovering finer image details. In this work, we propose a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based model tailored for IR image SR utilizing residual blocks, subpixel convolutions and batch normalization layers for efficient feature extraction and upscaling. The loss function incorporates perceptual loss to encourage realistic outputs and total variation (TV) loss to reduce noise and ensure smoothness while preserving edges. The proposed method is compared against state-of-the-art methods demonstrating superior performance in recovering high-quality IR images.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Intelligent IoT Communication System for Enhanced Security, Reliability, and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This research proposes a new approach for developing and implementing a smart communication system of IoT through developmental blockchain technology. Regarding the proposed solution, it is suggested that a distributed ledger can improve security, reliability, and efficiency of communication of IoT devices. They tackle issues such as data integrity, privacy and security in IoT networks as well as the problem of trust in such networks. The solution provides a decentralised and secure IoT ecosystem communication hence allowing monitoring, controlling and administration of the IoT build ecosystems in real time. Blockchain technology, however, when combined with nextgeneration communication interfaces and modern data analysis techniques, can offer various superior characteristics such as device identification, origin of information, etc. to IoT applications. It also enhances the dependability and capacity of IoT systems regarding capability and efficiency. Analysis and performance comparisons substantiate the performance benefits of the proposed intelligent communication system based on blockchain technology In addition these theoretical and performance analyses and experimental evaluation confirm the applicability and potential of the blockchain-based intelligent communication system to transform IoT communication models and facilitate the new generation of eIOT applications in a number of fields. The key to the solution to incorporate blockchain fundamental infrastructure to augment the communication channel of IoT devices. Using cryptography and consensus methodologies with the decentralized framework, integrity and confidentiality of the data is properly maintained because of the barriers of malicious interception or manipulation of the data. The communication system also boosts trust within the network participants because it offers a decentralized and immutable ledger of data transactions on the blockchain. Instead, one of the compelling benefits of this solution is that real-time monitoring, controlling, and management of the IoT systems can be made. This helps the stakeholders to closely monitor and manage the IoT deployments in a very efficient and enhanced manner the performance and reliability of the overall systems.

articleTitle: Hybrid ResNet-YOLOv5 Based Deep Learning Framework for Animal Monitoring in Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Precise and effective animal monitoring is essential for sustaining environmental equilibrium and wildlife preser-vation. This research introduces an innovative Hybrid ResNet-YOLOv5 deep learning (DL) architecture for real-time moni-toring of animals in various environments. The system utilizes ResNet's residual learning for feature extraction and combines it with the YOLOv5 object detection model for reliable identification and tracking of animals in their natural environments. The system is engineered to accommodate many species and environmental circumstances, providing reliable performance in difficult situations such as occlusions and poor illumination. Experimental findings indicate that the Hybrid ResNet-YOLOv5 architecture attains an accuracy of 95.4%, surpassing standard ResNet(92.1%), YOLO (90.6%), and LSTM (88.9%) models. The suggested technique exhibits exceptional precision (94.5%), recall (96.2%), and Fl-score (95.3%), rendering it highly effective for wildlife monitoring and conservation efforts.

articleTitle: Air Quality Monitoring System Using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Air quality deterioration is becoming a growing concern, impacting public health daily. Individuals residing in polluted environments face various health risks, making it essential for everyone to stay informed about the air quality in their surroundings. This paper presents a novel real-time air quality monitoring technique based on Arduino Uno technology. The system integrates multiple sensors, including the MQ135gas sensor, BMP180 atmospheric pressure sensors, and DHT11 humidity sensors to provide comprehensive environmental data. The system measures air pollution in parts per million(PPM) and displays live readings on an LCD screen while simultaneously transmitting data to a mobile device through a Bluetooth serial interface for remote monitoring. When pollutant levels exceed a predetermined threshold, a relay module activates an exhaust fan to improve air circulation and maintain a healthier environment. The MQ135 detects harmful greenhouses such as ammonia(NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), nitrogen oxides(NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>), carbon monoxide(CO), and carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), with an accuracy of ±5%. Additionally, the BMP180 sensor measures atmospheric pressure and temperature, while the DHT11 sensor records humidity, enhancing the system's overall precision. This study evaluates air quality in two distinct environments: (i) indoor and ii) outdoor settings. With its energy-efficient and cost-effective design, the proposed solution is ideal for monitoring air quality in residential and proportional spaces. By promoting better air quality management this system contributes to improved environmental conditions and raises public awareness of air pollution and its health impacts.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning for Improved Abstractive Sentence Summarization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Text summarizing aims to overview the material while maintaining essential details concisely. Lately, summary tasks have been included in the contrastive learning process in addition to visual representation. To optimize their similarities, contrastive learning summarizing algorithms currently concentrate on modelling and semantic similarity in all documents, targets, and data summaries. They do not, however, consider the impact that sentence semantics have on the text. In this study, we propose an RNN technique to develop the model for detecting the salient information. The sentence salience is based on the semantic similarity between the summary sentences of the original content, taking into account the distance of the loss of contrast in the form of soft weights functions. Consequently, our proposed model minimizes the semantic similarity given the textual summaries and possible noise and maximizes the semantic words between summaries and relevant information. Three popular datasets—multi news, CNN/Daily Mail, and Booksum datasets achieved the highest accuracy of 0.69% in the news datasets. The experiment outcomes demonstrate that the suggested strategy can considerably raise baseline performance and outperform other contrastive learning techniques.

articleTitle: Analysing the Impact of Dietary Habits on Cholesterol Levels: A Simulation-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: A shortened version of an abstract study on dietary habits as they relate to cholesterol levels, using simulation in Python. It generated synthetic data for 100 participants, including diet (red meat, fish, dairy, chocolate) and health (cholesterol, blood pressure, and weight) characteristics. Libraries such as NumPy, pandas, matplotlib, and seaborn have been used in data analysis and visualization. A correlation matrix showed highly significant associations between dietary patterns and health outcomes.

articleTitle: Efficient Human Activity Recognition through Multi-Sensor Data and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Extensive research takes place in the field of Human Activity Recognition (HAR) systems with wearable computing that helps in healthcare applications, fitness tracking and smart environments. Sensor technology advances have propelled Human Activity Recognition systems to utilize innovative machine learning methods for accurate and robust activity classification. This work evaluates the effectiveness of four cutting-edge deep learning models-Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU)-through their implementation on publicly accessible accelerometer and gyroscope HAR datasets. These classification models underwent testing through different activation functions namely ReLU, Leaky ReLU, and Swish to assess their practicality for classification operations. Standard evaluation metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, ROC-AUC and F1-score demonstrate the best features of each implemented model while providing descriptive visual representations. TCN delivered 98.59% accuracy and exhibited superior training speed efficiency thus establishing itself as the suitable AI algorithm for real-time implementation. This research offers an extensive breakdown for choosing optimal models in real-time HAR systems which supports advances in wearable computing and activity recognition technologies.

articleTitle: Creating An Effective Machine Learning Model For Monitoring And Maintaining Cardiac Health
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Heart disease causes many deaths each year, making it a major global health problem. To improve patient outcomes and reduce mortality, early detection and accurate diagnosis of heart disease are essential. When the coronary arteries become blocked, poor blood flow to the heart can be prevented, leading to coronary artery disease. Early detection of heart disease can reduce medical costs and potentially save the patient's life. Recently demonstrated methods have improved the accuracy of heart disease diagnosis in experimental data without compromising the accuracy of training data, but most of these algorithms suffer from the problem of redundancy. In this study, we develop a new analysis system to solve this problem, and the resulting system shows high recognition and good performance on both training and test data. Machine learning (ML) algorithms have shown the ability to help healthcare professionals make accurate and precise decisions. In this paper, based on the machine learning methods investigated, Decision Tree (DT) and Random Forest(RF), Using a bar graph, the accuracy of each is compared with each other.

articleTitle: A Scalable Auction Platform Using MERN
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The emergence of online auction platforms has revolutionized how individuals and businesses engage in a competitive digital market. This document outlines the design and implementation of a scalable auction platform utilizing the MERN (MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, Node.js) stack, emphasizing creating a seamless user experience, strong performance, and efficient scalability. The suggested platform incorporates real-time bidding features, secure payment systems, and a user-friendly interface to guarantee accessibility and engagement across various user groups. The platform is capable of accommodating high levels of concurrent user activity while maintaining data integrity and consistency by utilizing MongoDB's adaptable NoSQL architecture and the dynamic capabilities of React.js for the front end. Scalability is further enhanced through Node.js for server-side operations and Express.js for a modular backend design. This paper also addresses the architectural choices, performance enhancements, and challenges encountered during development. Findings from stress testing and user feedback underscore the platform's potential to challenge traditional auction systems, offering a strong, scalable solution for contemporary e-commerce needs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Driven Ultrasound Image Classification with Filter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Breast Cancer (BC) ranks being the most prevalent form of cancer, streessing the significance of accurate diagnosis a priority in medical research. Determine if a tumor is benign or malignant is crucial for effective treatment and reducing healthcare costs. Ultrasound imaging is a widely adopted method for breast tumor screening, but the presence of scattered noise in these images often hinders diagnostic accuracy, complicating radiologists efforts to detect abnormalities. This study emphasizes enhancing image quality as a preprocessing step before training machine learning models. To achieve this, the entropy of three filters, Gaussian, and Sobel, are evaluated for their ability to minimize noise and enhance edges. The filtered images are classified using Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The performance of these classifiers is assessed through metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall to determine the most effective approach for cell classification.

articleTitle: Orbiting Mouse for CAD Tools
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The Orbiting Mouse is the latest input device augmenting three-dimensional control in CAD, and its designer gave special consideration to user precision, ergonomic comfort, and operational efficiency. The main body details the design and implementation of such a device, which pairs an orbital control system with a triple-axis magnetometer, plus customizable function buttons targeting CAD applications. The proposed system greatly simplifies complex 3D manipulation, thus reducing fatigue as an interface integrates seamlessly with CAD applications in the industry. This proves to be an enlightening research study on architecture, application, and potential improvements with its application to contemporary digital design workflows.

articleTitle: Grid Technologies used in Solid State Transformers for Efficient Integration of Sustainable Energy Source
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The aim in this study is to use solid-state transformer-based converters to add renewable energy sources to smart grids. It looks at the advantages of this method, such as higher reliability, lower costs, and more speed. It also talks about the problems that come with putting these converters into action, like problems with power quality, harmonic content, and working with the grid infrastructure that is already in place. In the last part of the study, the authors talk about the need for more research in this area and how it might help make it easier to add renewable energy to smart grids. A complete plan is shown in this study for adding green energy sources to smart grids by using solid-state transformer-based converters. Simulation results are used to prove that the suggested model is correct. The findings show that the suggested method works very well and can be used to add renewable energy sources to smart grids as suggested.

articleTitle: An Automated Weed-Detection Approach Using Deep Learning in Agriculture System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Weed management is a critical factor in ensuring agricultural productivity, as weeds compete with crops for essential resources, significantly reducing yield quality and quantity. Traditional methods, such as manual weeding and indiscriminate herbicide application, are not only labour-intensive but also pose environmental hazards and escalate production costs. This paper introduces an advanced automated weed detection system designed to support precision agriculture by leveraging deep learning technologies. The system integrates DenseNet for high-accuracy binary classification and YOLO for real-time object detection and localization of weeds. DenseNet achieved a validation accuracy of 96%, effectively distinguishing between crop and weed images, while YOLO demonstrated a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 92%, accurately localizing weeds using bounding boxes. This dual-model approach provides an efficient, scalable, and environmentally sustainable solution for targeted weed control. Experimental results highlight its potential to significantly reduce herbicide dependency, optimize resource utilization, and facilitate automated farming practices. Future work will focus on enhancing dataset diversity, improving real-time deployment on drones and robots, and expanding system functionality to include crop health monitoring.

articleTitle: Optimization of Renewable Energy Resources using an Internet-of-Things and Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Energy power development and the heavy reliance on traditional sources are creating challenges for sustainable growth. Solar power offers a clean and promising alternative, but it is not without its own set of issues, such as intermittent supply and inefficiency. This paper introduces a smarter way to manage renewable energy: a system designed to combine solar energy generation, storage, and automated management to address these gaps. By using real-time monitoring and advanced technologies, such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Maximum PowerPoint Tracking (MPPT), the system helps users make the most of their energy. What makes it even better is its ability to send unused energy back to the grid after meeting household or industrial needs, thereby allowing users to earn subsidies to contribute to a cleaner energy network. This paper outlines a practical, forward-thinking approach to renewable energy that is not only about efficiency but also about creating a sustainable future for all.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Convolution Neural Network for Deforestation Risk Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Deforestation is a major danger to biodiversity, climate stability, and ecosystems. Accurately measuring and predicting the hazards associated with deforestation is critical for effective conservation and policymaking. This paper introduces a novel way to assess deforestation risk using Hierarchical Convolutional Neural Networks (HCNNs) driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI). The proposed model analyzes satellite imagery and environmental data hierarchically, learning geographical patterns and risk variables connected with deforestation activities. By including multi-scale feature extraction, the hierarchical CNN model yields strong predictions and risk assessments at various levels of detail, encompassing both macro and micro environmental changes. The model is trained and verified using real-world deforestation datasets, achieving an excellent accuracy of 98.9%, precision of 97.3%, recall of 96.0%, and F1-score of 96.6%, outperforming traditional machine learning (ML) methods.

articleTitle: Impact of Halo Doping on the Electrical Performance of Gate-All-Around Field Effect Transistors (GAAFETs)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This work deals with the performance of Gate-All-Around Field Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) as influenced by halo doping, wherein structural and electrical characteristics are explored. A comparative study is undertaken on GAAFET structures doped with halo and those not doped, from which primary observations are inferred based on the parameters of drain current, transconductance, and electric field distributions. Including halo doping introduces localized doping near the source and drain, enhancing electrostatic control, reducing leakage currents, and mitigating short-channel effects. Halo doping yields a greater subthreshold slope and better carrier confinement, as highlighted by sharper transitions in the drain current characteristics and a great decrease in offstate leakage. Transconductance analysis indicates that the gate control is effective, and current response is greater in drain current modulation. Also, electric field comparison highlights the stronger perpendicular and total electric fields near the critical regions, enhancing carrier confinement and increasing isolation between the source and drain. The results show that halo doping not only improves the performance metrics of GAAFETs, including drive current and switching efficiency, but also helps overcome the challenges associated with scaling. This work highlights the role of halo doping as a design approach for optimizing advanced transistor architectures and sheds light on its potential for next-generation low-power, high-performance electronic applications.

articleTitle: A Survey on Video Search Engine Technology: Advances in Video Processing, Speech Recognition, and Indexing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This paper is a comprehensive review of recent video search engine technology, focusing on three main areas: video processing, speech recognition, and indexing. With the rise of multimedia in various fields, there is a growing need to process, index, and retrieve video content based on user queries. This paper covers key advancements, including enhanced video frame extraction, natural language processing (NLP) for speech-to-text and indexing strategies for video search. It also discusses current challenges, existing solutions, and future directions and highlights the rapid evolution of video search technology.

articleTitle: Design of 4-Bit Multiplier Using Modified Gate Diffusion Input Technology for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Multipliers are widely used in digital circuits for countless arithmetic operations and are critical components in many very large scale integration systems. The multiplication process is one of the basic processes in digital equipment, and hardware multipliers play a key role in facilitating efficient data processing and fast computing. The demand for multipliers that are characterised by low energy consumption and high performance has stimulated the development of a variety of design methods, with particular emphasis on surface and energy efficiency. In this research we introduce a modified gate-diffusion input (MGDI) cell architecture for a 4-bit field multiplier that shows a higher energy efficiency than traditional designs of multipliers. The MGDI-based multiplier achieves a significant reduction in energy consumption (1.109861 mW) while maintaining the necessary operational efficiencies. The 4-bit MGDI multiplier is carefully designed using Tanner EDA tools, and extensive simulations have been performed to demonstrate its performance.

articleTitle: 3D CT Liver Images Lesion Extraction and Classification for Using 3D-CNN with GLRLM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The imaging technique known as computed tomography (CT) is often considered to be the most reliable way for non-invasive diagnosis. Through the use of three-dimensional (3D) computed tomography images, we were able to categorize aggressive tumors that were found in the liver for the aim of this research. When it comes to the three-dimensional (3D) CT image, the dimension reduction is accomplished by the use of principal component analysis (PCA). The Random Forest Algorithm is responsible for identifying the abnormal hepatic region, and a median filter is used to reduce the amount of noise occurring. Methods of data augmentation are also employed in this process. To extract Gray Level Run Length Matrix (GLRLM) features, using Pyradiomics python package. These features are then fed into a 3D-CNN classifier to classify malignant tumors and haemangiomas. Our model was found to have greater performance after being compared to the findings of other models. This was revealed after the comparison was made. For the training dataset, our model has an accuracy of 97.2%, and for the test dataset, it has an accuracy of 98.25%. This accuracy is determined by the performance metrics that our model incorporates.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Traffic-Driven Services Provisioning in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The increasing demand for high-capacity and dynamic services in optical networks necessitates intelligent and adaptive provisioning mechanisms. This study investigates the application of machine learning (ML) techniques for traffic-driven service provisioning in optical networks, addressing challenges such as traffic prediction, resource allocation, and fault management. The proposed framework employs supervised and unsupervised learning models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Random Forests, and K-Means clustering, to analyze traffic patterns and optimize service deployment. The system leverages real-time and historical traffic data to predict demand, enabling proactive resource allocation and dynamic wavelength assignment. Furthermore, reinforcement learning is explored to automate decision- making for adaptive routing and spectrum management under varying network conditions. Performance evaluation on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrates that ML-based approaches significantly improve network efficiency, reduce latency, and enhance the quality of service (QoS). This research highlights the potential of machine learning in revolutionizing service provisioning in optical networks, offering scalable, data-driven solutions to meet the growing demands of next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: Automated Hydrogen Peroxide Flow Control for Optimized Paper Bleaching in Paper Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The amount and control of chemical additives, including hydrogen peroxide, determine the effectiveness and ecological implications of bleaching techniques for paper. Conventional application processes of hydrogen peroxide during the bleaching stage of paper production tend to provide variable bleaching effects and high consumption of the additive. Such factors are of utmost significance in maintaining product quality as well as minimizing operational costs. This paper discusses an automated system in controlling the flow of hydrogen peroxide, objectives to improve the paper bleaching process effectively and uniformly distribute a chemical additive. In our approach, we couple sophisticated flow control technology with real-time monitoring systems that adjust the flows dynamically based on specific needs of the bleaching process. Sensors continuously measure critical process variables, while maintaining optimal concentration of peroxide at all times with controlled feedback loops. Such automation ensures more precise chemical dosing, results in more uniform bleaching, and paper of better quality. Such a control system for an automated flow significantly improves the efficiency of bleaching compared with conventional systems. It helps in achieving more even brightness in paper and reduces the level of chemicals used in the system, thereby making production environmentally sustainable since chemical waste becomes less and probably negative impacts on the environment decrease.

articleTitle: An Explainable Artificial Intelligence Model to Detect Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The death rate of women has been increasing rapidly over the years due to carcinoma of the female breast. Every year, more than two million female get news that they have breast cancer, according to cancer research. Thus, early diagnosis and treatment can only reduce the death rate, which leads to a long life. It is crucial to classify tumors correctly; in that case, the machine-learning technique plays a vital role. Explainable AI is aiding in obtaining trust in the ML model by clarifying the decision-making process. This work has applied six different classifiers to the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Diagnostic dataset for breast cancer detection. Additionally, in order to evaluate the model's forecast and comprehend the significance of the features in its result, this study employed SHAP and LIME analysis to the logistic regression model. The best model was selected after evaluating and comparing the results of different performance matrices. Out of all the classifiers, Support Vector Machine and Logistic Regression had the best accuracy (98%).

articleTitle: Friction Stir Welding Dissimilar AA-5083 and AA-6061 Alloys with Fuzzy Logic and Enhanced MLP Predictive Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The joining of dissimilar aluminum alloys, such as AA-5083 and AA-6061, via Friction Stir Welding (FSW) presents significant challenges due to differences in their material properties. This study proposes a predictive model combining Fuzzy Logic and an Enhanced Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural network to optimize the FSW process for these alloys. The model aims to predict key welding parameters, such as tensile strength and hardness, based on input variables including tool rotational speed, welding speed, and plunge depth. The Fuzzy Logic system captures the non-linear and uncertain relationships between process parameters, while the Enhanced MLP refines these predictions through a robust learning process. Experimental data was collected for various welding conditions, and the model's performance was evaluated against actual results. The proposed model demonstrated high accuracy in predicting the mechanical properties of the welded joints, providing valuable insights for improving the quality and reliability of FSW joints in dissimilar AA-5083 and AA-6061 alloys. This approach can be used to optimize welding parameters in real-world applications, offering a tool for manufacturers to achieve superior weld quality while minimizing defects.

articleTitle: Explainable AI (XAI) Using SHAP and LIME for Financial Fraud Detection and Credit Scoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Financial fraud detection and credit scoring are two important applications in the financial domain on which high accuracy and interpretability are required. While Random Forests and XGBoost algorithms of the third generation produce good prediction quality, there is no way to explain the prediction results and they do not meet transparency criteria of regulators. The work in this paper focuses on the incorporation of Explainable AI (XAI) methods such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to combat these issues of concern under trust, compliance and accountability within these models. Decision Trees were employed for the detection of fraud while Random Forest was employed for credit scoring, SHAP was used for global feature importance and LIME for instance explanations. The model for fraud detection had accuracy of 95% and SHAP found the characteristics of transactions such as amount and frequency significant for fraud detection, While, the credit scoring model that had 76% accuracy and with the help of LIME, the debt ratios and payment history of the credit contenders was found important. The integration of SHAP and LIME improves the model interpretability and fairness, and makes the stakeholders and regulating authorities to trust AI solutions that will be used in the future of financial companies.

articleTitle: Red Deer Optimization Algorithm-Based RSUs Deployment Method for Maximizing Network Coverage in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In the intelligent transportation systems (ITS), roadside units (RSUs) need to be deployed strategically in vehicular ad hoc network (VANETs) for facilitating a pivotal entity which helps in potential interactions among vehicles. A well deployed RSUs methodology is determined to improved the quality of service since it helps in minimizing the financial costs with low deployment costs and maximized range of transmission. In this paper, Red Deer Optimization Algorithm-based RSUs deployment method is proposed as a adaptive strategy which helped in maximizing the network coverage in VANETs with flexible traffic demands. This RDOARDS approach considered the requirements of service and economic feasibility for improving the characteristics of traffic flow, road network topology and information coverage. It employed the merits of Red Deer Optimization Algorithm (RDOA) for the objective of determining the optimal points in the network over which the RSUs need to be positioned for maximized network coverage in VANETs. The results of this RDOARDS approach confirmed better coverage rate and minimized RSUs deployments compared to the baseline approached for the objective of improving the service quality and boosting network connectivity.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Efficacy of Machine Learning-Based Intrusion Detection Systems on an Imbalanced and Contemporary Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: As the Internet has increased in popularity, more computers are networked and becoming part of our daily lives. Common and less evident server vulnerabilities may be used by hackers to access systems and conduct complicated assaults. An Intrusion Detection System (IDs), a popular computer security tool, uses machine learning on a previously acquired dataset. The datasets were generated in distinct networks across brief periods and may not contain the latest information. They're bloated and can't hold enough data to survive an attack. Modern intrusion detection systems are less effective with inconsistent and outdated information for rare attack paths. This paper presents five machine-learning intrusion detection solutions. K Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Gradient Boosting (GB), Adaboost (AB), and Random Forest (RF) are used. The latest security dataset CSE-CIC-IDS2018 replaces earlier, more often-used datasets to improve Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). An unbalanced dataset was selected. The imbalance ratio is reduced using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), a synthetic data model. The approach increases attack type-specific system performance while lowering false alarms and missing incursions. Minor classes increase their data amounts to reach the average data size. Experimental results demonstrate that the recommended strategy greatly enhances uncommon intrusion detection.

articleTitle: SMART EYES: Deep Learning-Driven Animal Detection and Alerting System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Human encroachment into natural habitats has intensified human-wildlife conflicts, necessitating effective, real-time solutions to monitor animal activities and mitigate risks. This project, Smart Eyes, presents a cost-effective animal detection and alerting system utilizing the ATmega328P microcontroller, USB-to-TTL communication, and a buzzer. It integrates deep learning with hardware for robust performance in detecting and managing interactions with wildlife. The system employs the YOLOv5 (You Only Look Once, version 5) algorithm, renowned for its real-time object detection capabilities, to accurately identify animals such as elephants and cheetahs. Pretrained and fine-tuned on a comprehensive dataset, YOLOv5 ensures high precision by minimizing false detections—the ATmega328P processes detection signals, while the USB-to-TTL interface facilitates seamless communication with external devices. Alerts are generated via a buzzer, enabling prompt responses to wildlife intrusions. Designed for deployment in regions prone to human-wildlife conflict, this system reduces dependency on manual monitoring methods like camera traps or field observation. It enhances conservation efforts by providing real-time data, enabling proactive management, and safeguarding both human and animal populations. This project offers a scalable, efficient, and reliable solution for wildlife monitoring, addressing critical challenges in conservation and human-wildlife coexistence.

articleTitle: Crop Disease Analysis with Different Classification Models using Orange Data Mining Tool
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the principal economic activities of the India on agriculture for their livelihood. This study presents a crop disease prediction system utilizing the Orange data mining tool to analyze image datasets of diseased plant leaves from various fruits and vegetables, including apple, strawberry, blueberry, cherry, corn, and potato. The system employs machine learning algorithms to classify and predict crop diseases through the analysis of leaf images. Includes an image data set comprising various healthy and unhealthy crop leaves. Image dataset containing different healthy and unhealthy crop leaves was collected and preprocessed. Multiple classification models, including Image Embedding, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, KNN, Tree, SVM,Neural Networks [1] Scatter Plot, ROC Analysis, Confusion Matrix,are implemented in the Orange environment. The model underwent training using 80% of the dataset, while the remaining 20% was utilized for validation. The results indicated that the Supervised Learning model attained the highest level of accuracy in recognizing and categorizing crop diseases based on leaf images. This system offers farmers an effective means for the early detection of diseases, facilitating prompt intervention and potentially minimizing crop losses. Future efforts will concentrate on broadening the image dataset and integrating more crop varieties to improve the system's adaptability and precision.

articleTitle: Integrating Behavioral Analytics and AI for Enhanced Academic Performance Prediction Using Graph Convolution Networks and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The work explores the integration of behavioral analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, specifically Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and deep learning, to predict student academic performance.
