By analyzing study habits, assignment submissions, gaming behavior, and exam scores, the framework bridges traditional evaluation methods and behavioral insights. Results demonstrate that a GCN model outperforms other machine learning approaches, achieving a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 117.97. The findings highlight the potential of machine learning to enhance educational strategies, identify at-risk students, and provide actionable insights for data-driven educational improvements.

articleTitle: Innovative Air Quality Monitoring with K-Means Algorithm and Smart Sensor Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Air pollution is a growing concern worldwide, with detrimental effects on human health and living conditions. The increasing interest in air quality assessment has led to numerous projects initiated by civil society and individuals aiming to locally evaluate air quality, especially in heavily polluted regions like northern India. The work is based on the implementation of a real-time atmospheric air quality monitoring system that integrates multiple sensors to measure parameters such as CO2, SO2, NO, NH3, O3, PM2.5, PM10, temperature, humidity, and dissolved oxygen. The sensor data is processed by a microcontroller, utilizing both Arduino and motherboard components, with results displayed on an LCD screen and transmitted to a laptop. To enhance the analysis of collected data, the K-Means clustering algorithm is employed to identify patterns and classify air quality conditions. This approach allows for the categorization of pollution levels, providing valuable insights into air quality trends. The proposed calibration method demonstrates the system's effectiveness, showcasing its ability to achieve sensitivity and granulometric resolution comparable to more sophisticated instruments. This comprehensive system bridges the gap between technical precision and social relevance, offering a powerful tool for monitoring and disseminating crucial air quality information to end-users. The integration of K-Means clustering further enriches the system's capability to provide actionable insights for addressing air pollution challenges.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Sound Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In this article discusses about the new sound wave energy harvester based on piezoelectric materials for sustainable low-voltage applications. Urban and industrial noise, although it is a renewable energy source, poses challenges in efficient harvesting due to variable sound frequencies and intensities. The proposed system is designed to overcome these challenges by selectively converting ambient noise into electrical power. The harvester possesses an on/off AI-driven control, which is based on machine learning algorithms to provide optimal sound conditions and can only activate the device in these conditions. Tests of 35–100 dB and 60–500 Hz ranges demonstrated peak output at 69 Hz with 3.2 V, 3.2 mA, and 10.24 mW. This type of adaptive control increases efficiency, saves energy, and extends the lifetime of a device since it works under set conditions. This project offers a promising, eco-friendly solution to low-power applications by selectively capturing sound energy in noise-rich environments, contributing to innovative AI optimization for sustainable energy technologies.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Optimization Deep Learning Frame Work for Efficient Stock Market Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The widespread need to forecast future market trends has prompted the incorporation of cutting-edge technology that go beyond the realm of conventional statistical models. Predicting the future of the stock market using ML and DL methods is the focus of this article. We offer a holistic strategy that incorporates effective methods for feature selection, data preparation, and classification. To clean up the data and lower the noise level, the wavelet transform technique is used. By determining which input features are most important, the Dandelion-Optimization-Algorithm(DOA) optimizes feature selection. An innovative model for analyzing stock market data is created, 3DCNN-GRU, which combines a 3DCNNwith a gated-recurrent-unit(GRU). The Blood-Coagulation-Algorithm(BCA) makes it easier to tune hyperparameters, which improves the performance of the model. The outstanding prediction accuracy of 99.14% achieved by our methodology demonstrates its durability and efficacy in stock market anticipating applications. The proposed model has a lot of potential, but it can only handle the Nifty 50 index because that's all the dataset covers. The work's broader implications imply that the model might be further validated and its applicability improved by including additional datasets and investigating alternative market conditions. To guarantee robustness and generalizability, future research could concentrate on using this model in different financial circumstances.

articleTitle: Alzheimer's Disease Detection Using Ensemble Techniques on MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a significant diagnostic challenge as well as the leading cause of dementia. MRI scans can reveal structural brain changes, but the manual interpretation of these scans is both subjective and time intensive. This work therefore explores an automated approach using deep learning to detect Alzheimer's from MRI images. It proposes an ensemble of three models - EfficientNet, Vision Transformer (ViT), and SqueezeNet which were each chosen for its unique strengths in image analysis. EfficientNet excels in feature extraction, ViT captures long-range dependencies within images, and SqueezeNet offers computational efficiency. These models were then trained to identify four stages of cognitive decline: Non-Demented, Very Mild Demented, Mild Demented, and Moderate Demented. By utilizing the complementary strengths of these architectures, our ensemble approach achieved an impressive 90.50% accuracy on a publicly available Kaggle dataset, outperforming individual models. This paper demonstrates both the potential of combining diverse deep learning architectures and also presents a promising step towards enhancing both the accuracy and efficiency of Alzheimer's detection from MRI images.

articleTitle: AI Based Mock Interview System Using Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Mock interviews are crucial for job applicants to enhance and polish their skills before to real interviews. This study presents a novel AI-driven Mock Interview System that replicates authentic interview settings through the utilization of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Deep Learning, and Computer Vision. The system incorporates Speech-to-Text for response processing, Text-to-Speech for feedback dissemination, and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for the adaptive assessment of response precision. Employing OpenCV and MediaPipe, it examines behaviors such as facial expressions, ocular movements, and additional non-verbal signals. The system produces domain-specific questions, assesses fluency, coherence, and content, and delivers comprehensive feedback on linguistic skills, technical knowledge, and professional conduct. Experimental findings indicate 95% accuracy in verbal communication analysis, 93% precision in behavioral assessment, and a 90% user satisfaction rating. The solution transcends conventional mock interview constraints, guaranteeing scalability, personalization, and immediate feedback, thereby enabling job seekers to refine their skills and bolster their confidence for successful interviews.

articleTitle: Optimized Vision Transformer with Adaptive Attention for High-Precision Skin Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This work presents an effective Vision Transformer model with Adaptive Learning and Normalization (ViT-ALN), applied to skin cancer classification with the HAM10000 set. To enhance the feature extraction and learning, the authors employ GELU activation, Layer Normalization, and Dropout in the construction of ViT-ALN. The model was trained on re-scaled and augmented images and the model successfully established a classification protocol. In this study, ViT-ALN has a classification accuracy of 96.8% higher than most traditional CNN architectures. These were performed over 250 iterations and led to marked improvements in the ability to distinguish between benign and malignant skin lesions. From these results, it is corroborated that ViT-ALN architecture improvement brings better diagnostic performance for serving the clinical need in dermatology.

articleTitle: IOT-Enabled CNG Tank Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The CNG Tank Monitoring System is designed to enhance the safety, efficiency, and reliability of compressed natural gas (CNG) storage and management. It integrates advanced sensors, automation technologies, and real-time data processing to provide comprehensive monitoring and control of CNG tank conditions. Specifically tailored for industrial and vehicular applications, the system continuously tracks critical parameters such as tank levels, temperature, and gas pressure. By identifying and addressing anomalies swiftly, it reduces the risks associated with pressurized gas storage, such as leaks, overpressure, and overheating. The hardware includes temperature, pressure, and level sensors interfaced with a Raspberry Pi microcontroller, which processes real-time data to trigger safety measures when thresholds are breached. For instance, if the system detects overpressure, it activates venting mechanisms to release excess gas, preventing accidents. The software features a centralized dashboard that provides real-time monitoring and alerts both locally and remotely. It also supports cloud integration for remote access, data storage, and predictive analytics. Key outputs obtained from the system include effective pressure monitoring, which quickly detects anomalies such as overpressure or leaks, and temperature analysis that identifies overheating conditions. Gas concentration sensors have successfully detected leaks exceeding 5% methane concentration, with automated safety actions triggered within 2 seconds. Historical data analysis has optimized maintenance scheduling, reducing downtime by 15%. This system not only ensures safety but also promotes operational efficiency and proactive management of CNG tanks, making it an essential tool for modern gas storage and distribution systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing IoT Service Placement in Fog Computing Environments Using Deep Q Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has created an urgent need for efficient service scheduling strategies in fog computing environments (FCEs), where computational resources are distributed across edge nodes. Traditional service placement methods often struggle to balance latency, energy consumption, and resource utilization. In this research, we deliver a new method for optimizing IoT service placement using Deep Q Networks (DQN), a reinforcement learning technique that can dynamically learn optimal placement strategies based on real-time network conditions. Our model continuously evaluates the state of the fog environment, including factors such as node load, bandwidth availability, and service demands, to intelligently place IoT services in a way that minimizes latency and maximizes resource efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DQN-based placement strategy outperforms conventional heuristic and rule-based methods in terms of latency reduction, energy savings, and overall system performance.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Network Security Using Unsupervised Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This study presents an innovative methodology employing GNNs for network intrusion detection, utilizing the KDD Cup 1999 dataset, a well-established standard for assessing intrusion detection systems. The dataset encompasses a diverse array of simulated assaults and legitimate connections, consisting of 41 attributes for each connection record. We utilize stringent data preparation methods and develop a graph representation of the network data to enhance the GNN model. The experimental findings indicate that the suggested GNN surpasses conventional classifiers, with an accuracy of 93.7%, a precision of 92%, and an Fl-score of 91.5%. These metrics indicate substantial enhancements compared to KNN, SVM, CNN, and RNN models. The results indicate that GNNs proficiently capture intricate linkages within network data, improving the capacity to detect hostile activity. This research advances cybersecurity by offering a strong and effective solution for real-time intrusion detection, emphasizing the efficacy of GNNs in combating increasingly sophisticated network threats and enhancing digital security.

articleTitle: Explainable Credit Score Risk Analysis: Integrating Outlier Detection and Ensemble Modelling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In this research, we have explored the complex field of credit risk prediction using a various approach that integrates machine learning model for classification and model explainability. Accurate risk assessment, model performance evaluation, and open communication of predictions to stakeholders are the main goals. The project begins with descriptive statistics and exploratory data analysis (EDA), which reveals information on the financial and demographic makeup of credit applicants. Afterwards, outlier identification and elimination through Tukey's method and IsolationForest are done separately to guarantee the validity of ensuing analyses. Our predictive modelling is based on the use of many techniques, including random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, logistic regression and finally ensemble model. Every model is fine-tuned for peak performance, and a comparative analysis provides a standard for forecast accuracy. We use methods such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to improve the interpretability of our models. With the use of these techniques, we can better understand and convey the judgments rendered by intricate models, promoting openness in the evaluation of credit risk.

articleTitle: Hybrid Gradient Descent and Sea Lion Optimization Algorithm (H-GD-SLnO) to Optimize Task Scheduling in Fog Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The architectures associated with cloud and fog computing are fundamentally important for the decentralization of computational tasks, as they facilitate the efficient processing of various user demands while simultaneously supporting extensive Internet of Things (IoT) networks that are increasingly prevalent in today's technological landscape. As the complexity and scale of computational loads continue to expand at a rapid pace, it becomes imperative to implement effective task scheduling mechanisms across these heterogeneous architectures, as this is vital for the optimization of resource utilization and the significant reduction of latency that can adversely affect system performance. This Paper centers on optimization, highlighting the novel integration of Gradient Descent (GD) and the Sea Lion Optimization Algorithm (SLnO). It proposes a harmonious methodology for addressing task scheduling challenges in Fog Computing by utilizing the accuracy of GD for localized searches and the exploratory strengths of SLnO for overarching optimization. The hybrid methodology (H-GD-SLnO) was evaluated using synthetic datasets and real grid workloads, including DAS-2 and AuverGrid, as well as Hadoop tasks like Terasort. The simulation outcomes reveal that (H-GD-SLnO) surpasses numerous pre-existing algorithms, realizing reductions in mean job completion time as well as average scheduling delay and enhancements in resource utilization and throughput. These results emphasize the efficacy of our proposed methodology in meeting the rigorous task scheduling demands within cloud and fog computing environments.

articleTitle: VETCARE+: A Deep Learning Application for Early Detection of Lameness in Dairy Cattle
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Lameness in dairy cattle indeed appears to be a prevalent and pertinent issue that impacts the welfare of the animals themselves and the economic viability of farms in general. This paper presents a new deep learning method tailored to the task of accomplishing on-time lameness detection in dairy cattle. It does so effectively by combining multiple sensor data with high level behavioural analysis, which forms the crux of nature. We aim to create a state-ofthe-art system that can detect using an integration of a wide range of sources of data, including but not limited to accelerometer, advanced computer vision, automated behavioural pattern recognition and milking robots’ data. We believe the new system should identify it with even more accuracy and at a significantly higher speed than current methods could attain so far. For the ambitious objective followed by this approach, we are using a multi-modal deep neural network as the central component of this proposed system. It leverages a set of several advanced features, including the latest notions of transfer learning and attention mechanisms, which enable it to utilize and make the most of a variety of data types. Initial trials conducted so far have shown that our advanced system is able to predict lameness with an impressive accuracy rate of 92%. At such a level of prediction, it can be done up to ten days ahead of what might have been determined by the traditional, visual methods used so far, without a substantially high false positive rate at merely 3%. These therefore hold much promise and with these expectations, great improvements will be witnessed both in the welfare of the dairy cattle and that of the farms in terms of productivity. This will be through early interventions and effective treatments of cases of lameness that may arise.

articleTitle: Optimized Electricity Price Prediction for Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: With the growing integration of renewable energy sources and the deregulation of electricity markets, electricity prices have become increasingly volatile, complicating accurate price forecasting. This volatility is especially significant for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), which rely on price predictions to schedule their charging and discharging cycles and maximize market arbitrage opportunities. Traditional prediction models often focus on minimizing the prediction error, which quantifies the difference between predicted and actual prices. However, this approach does not necessarily lead to optimal decision-making in BESS operations. Instead of focusing solely on prediction accuracy, the BESS's objective is to optimize its charging/discharging schedule to maximize benefits from price fluctuations, which involves minimizing the decision error—the gap between the optimal decisions based on predicted prices and those based on true market prices. This paper proposes a “predict, then optimize” framework, where accurate price predictions are integrated into a BESS scheduling model. The framework aims to reduce decision errors and enhance the arbitrage potential for BESS, contributing to more efficient energy storage management and better market performance. The research discusses various price prediction models and highlights the importance of aligning prediction strategies with the actual objectives of BESS operations to achieve superior financial outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancing Marine Resource Management with AI-Enabled Decision-Making and Policy Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Marine resource management encounters issues like overfishing, pollution, and ecological deterioration. It utilizes AI-driven models to tackle these challenges by using real-time data from maritime sensors, satellite photos, and historical records. Utilized methodologies include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for ecosystem predictions, reinforcement learning for sustainable fishing limits, and regression models for pollution detection. Results indicate substantial enhancements: forecast accuracy attained 92.5%, overfishing reduction escalated from 12.3% to 35.6%, pollution detection speed advanced from 48 to 8 hours, and fleet efficiency climbed from 67.4% to 85.2%. AI-driven decision support systems (DSS) significantly improved policy implementation duration, decreasing it from 20 to 5 days. These findings illustrate the efficacy of AI in advancing sustainability and economic viability in managing marine resources. Subsequent efforts will enhance the models and augment the dataset for comprehensive ecological monitoring and policy-making incorporation.

articleTitle: Cloud-Hosted AI Solutions in Virtual Reality for Pain Distraction and Management in Clinical Settings
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) settings that use cloud-hosted artificial intelligence (AI) systems have shown encouraging promise for the distraction and treatment of pain in healthcare settings. This study delves into creating and implementing an AI system on the cloud to improve VR experiences for those dealing with chronic pain or going through invasive medical procedures. The AI system adjusts the VR information in real-time based on the user's pain reactions and preferences, using the cloud's scalability and processing capacity. VR spaces are designed to give patients relaxing and engaging experiences, taking their minds off their discomfort. Patients who used these VR solutions improved with AI reported much lower levels of pain and anxiety, according to clinical research. The cloud-based method facilitates a resilient and adaptable pain management solution by ensuring smooth updates, ongoing learning from patient data, and remote access for healthcare providers. The system's architecture, the methods for assessing pain responses in real-time, and the findings from preliminary clinical trials. In various medical settings, the results indicate that cloud-hosted AI solutions in VR are a practical and efficient way to improve patient comfort and pain management.

articleTitle: Smart Transportation Revolution: Adaptive Monitoring with Squeeze and Excitation Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In the rapidly advancing field of smart cities, effective traffic management is essential for improving safety, alleviating congestion, and minimizing environmental damage. This paper rigorously examines the function of deep learning in adaptive traffic monitoring and presents an innovative method utilizing Squeeze and Excitation Networks (SENets). SENets enhance traffic monitoring systems by dynamically recalibrating feature maps, allowing for the prioritization of important features and hence boosting detection accuracy in intricate urban settings. The suggested system combines real-time data from IoT sensors, security cameras, and vehicular networks, offering a comprehensive framework for traffic monitoring and accident prevention. Experimental findings indicate that the SENets-based model attains a 94.5% accuracy in identifying traffic abnormalities and enhances signal control optimization by 30% relative to traditional methods. These findings highlight the capacity of SENets to transform urban traffic management, providing a scalable and economical solution for intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Optimization and Resource Allocation (AORA) Model for IoT-Edge Computing Using Hybrid Newton-Raphson and Dolphin Echolocation Algorithm (HNR-DEA) Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The swift expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) applications demands the implementation of real-time data processing and low-latency communication, thereby posing challenges to conventional cloud computing paradigms. This study confronts these issues by amalgamating edge computing with hybrid optimization methodologies, and introduces the AORA (Adaptive Optimization and Resource Allocation) framework. The AORA framework capitalizes on intelligent task scheduling, dynamic resource allocation, and energy-efficient approaches to augment the performance of edge computing.Our research methodology encompasses the collection and preprocessing of data derived from IoT devices, feature extraction, prediction of resource demand, and the optimization of task offloading. It employs the Hybrid Newton Raphson and Dolphin Echolocation Algorithm (HNR-DEA) methodology, which synergizes Newton Raphson optimization technique for faster convergence rate around local optima with bio-inspired Dolphin Echolocation Algorithm (DEA) for comprehensive global exploration.The Experimental outcomes reveal considerable advancements, including a 45% reduction in average latency, a 38% decrease in overall energy consumption, and a 23% enhancement in resource utilization. Furthermore, the model attained a 97% task completion rate alongside consistently elevated network throughput. Simulations were executed in CloudSim with 100 IoT devices generating dynamic workloads and edge servers equipped with multi-core processors. The experimental framework utilized Google Cluster Data to replicate workload variations, thereby ensuring scalability and robustness. These results underscore the AORA model's potential as a resilient and scalable solution for real-time IoT applications.

articleTitle: Gaussian Mixture Model and Independent Component Analysis for Time varying Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Clustering multivariate time series (MTS) by incorporating the related-evolving pattern and identifying common behaviors across various fields like data science, bioinformatics, finance, economics and environmental science are the central role for improving clustering results. Even though clustering time series data has been extensively studied in the past eras, no sufficient consideration has been paid to seizure time-varying association patterns in MTS. We recommend an innovative approach for clustering MTS data based on time-varying parameters. The proposed method introduces an unsupervised learning approach using Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to explain the related well-defined model between MTS features and generate time-varying variable identification problem as an optimized result, which enables the appropriate learning algorithm based on correlated block matric coordinates. Additionally, we apply the Independent Component Analysis (ICA) method on high-dimensional sequences to achieve low-dimensional feature vectors, and implement an effective structure for temporal based clustering approach to identify cluster with real world data-set. We incorporate wide experiments to compare the planned approach with 2 different clustering algorithms based on an open MTS dataset, which express that GMM meaningfully outperforms with improved efficiency on a diversity of clustering performance metrics.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Wireless Networks: Advancements in Hybrid Beamforming for Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Large-scale wireless communication systems are key enablers of next-generation networks, offering substantial improvements in capacity and data rates. However, the complexity and cost associated with these systems, particularly when implementing fully digital beamforming, present significant challenges. Reinforcement Learning (RL), a branch of machine learning, offers a novel and effective solution to address these challenges by dynamically optimizing beamforming strategies. This paper investigates the effectiveness of applying RL to three major beamforming architectures-analog, digital, and hybrid beamforming, with a primary focus on hybrid beamforming. RL frameworks allow the beamforming direction to be dynamically adjusted based on real-time feedback from channel state information (CSI). Through iterative learning, RL agents optimize system performance, adapting to varying channel conditions and minimizing power consumption. In hybrid beamforming, antennas share a single radio frequency (RF) chain, contrasting with digital beamforming where each antenna is connected to an individual RF chain. RL algorithms, such as Q-learning and deep reinforcement learning (DRL), are employed to select optimal beamforming weights, reducing computational complexity and enhancing energy efficiency while maintaining high data rates. This research evaluates the performance of RL-driven large-scale wireless communication systems across key metrics, including bit error rate (BER), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), achievable sum rate, power consumption, and energy efficiency. By leveraging RL, the system learns to balance performance and complexity, achieving significant improvements over conventional methods. A detailed comparison of the three beamforming techniques is provided, highlighting the enhanced adaptability and efficiency of RL-driven hybrid beamforming. The findings demonstrate that RL-based hybrid beamforming achieves an optimal trade-off between performance and complexity, making it a promising solution for next-generation wireless networks. Furthermore, the study underscores the critical role of optimizing CSI acquisition and RL parameter tuning to maximize system performance while minimizing energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Novel Hierarchical Crayfish Auto-Associative Polynomial Network-based Signal Degradation Prediction for Reliable Communication in Urban VANETs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Buildings are important in an urban Vehicular Ad Hoc Network (VANET) environment because they might serve as barriers that weaken the signal. These barriers result in multipath effects, which can significantly affect data transmission because of fading. As a result, measuring how buildings affect transmission quality is an important propagation model component, particularly in rescue circumstances where dependable communication is crucial. Based on the obstacles that moving emergency vehicles perceive in their environments, this study proposed a Hierarchical Crayfish auto-associative Polynomial Network (HCAPN), a hybrid of Hierarchical Auto associative Polynomial Network architecture and crayfish optimization, to create a predictive model that can estimate the degree of signal degradation, represented by the Bit Error Rate (BER). For the improved prediction, the input data was generated using correlation coefficients and min-max normalization. The model's higher prediction efficiency was demonstrated by its extremely low 1.35×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>RMSE, 1.82×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> MSE,1.12×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>MAE, and 5.67×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> MaxPE values when compared to the current models. Its ability to learn, generalize, and accurately forecast the BER for a new data instance was demonstrated by the results of the HCAPN simulation. All things considered, the study helps to improve the effectiveness and dependability of communication in urban VANET.

Author Keywords: Hierarchical Auto associative Polynomial Network architecture

articleTitle: Air Quality Analysis and Prediction in Tamil Nadu: AN ANN and CNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Air quality poses a significant environmental and health challenge, particularly in developing nations like India. Tamil Nadu, situated in southern India, grapples with severe air pollution issues stemming from diverse sources like discharges from automobiles, production tasks, biomass burning, and dust storms. Traditional monitoring and forecasting methods like ground-based stations and satellite observations have limitations concerning spatial and temporal coverage, cost, and upkeep. Consequently, there arises a demand for alternative approaches harnessing advancements in machine learning and big data analytics to furnish high-resolution, real-time air quality insights. In this study, we introduce an innovative methodology for analyzing and predicting air quality in Tamil Nadu employing artificial neural networks (ANNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). These sophisticated machine learning techniques adeptly capture intricate nonlinear relationships from extensive and diverse datasets while adeptly handling missing and noisy data. Leveraging historical datasets encompassing air pollutant concentrations, meteorological variables, and land use features sourced from multiple channels, we train and validate our models. We conduct comparative assessments with established methodologies, assessing our models' robustness and generalizability. Furthermore, we offer an understanding of the spatiotemporal dynamics and trends of air quality in Tamil Nadu, identifying pivotal factors and drivers of air pollution. Our proposed approach holds promise for policymakers, researchers, and the general populace to comprehend and ameliorate the air quality scenario not only in Tamil Nadu but also in analogous regions worldwide. Additionally, our model yields the following performance metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE): 0.037, R-squared (R2): 0.9998, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): 0.4522.

articleTitle: Plant Diseases Detection and Soil Quality Identification Techniques for Agriculture Professionals
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)

authors.preferredName: M. A. Y. Peer Mohamed Appa

abstract: Human civilization requires food production. Plant leaves and harvesting illnesses affected scientists' soil quality assessments. Plagues slow species growth. The right disease classification may reduce plant damage. Many diseases are hard to classify. Farmers misinterpret soil and plant leaf diseases. Hand-made soil quality and pathogen estimates are difficult. Without soil quality monitoring and plant disease classification, agricultural goods might be severely destroyed. Image processing may boost agricultural yield. Several methods utilize images of damaged leaves or crops to diagnose plant diseases and soil quality. Research has improved sickness categorization and diagnosis in several ways. Recent statements, actions, and debates need more. Global farming uses technology. CNN and ANN are artificial neural networks. Deep or traditional Machine Learning (ML) relies on the issue, data, and computing power. When processing and data resources are available, deep learning (DL), which uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and artificial neural networks (ANNs), is used for several challenging visual identification and classification tasks. It excels on its own datasets but struggles on others. This study's data, assessment criteria, and conclusions will help plant leaf and crop detection and soil quality measuring researchers.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Diabetic Retinopathy from Retinal Fundus Images Using Internet of Things and AI Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In recent times, the computer vision (CV) then Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have proven their worth across a range of applications, with a notable focus on healthcare. IoT-driven healthcare resolutions present intelligent strategies to significantly reduce costs and elevate the quality of healthcare services. Concurrently, Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) stands as a condition capable of causing permanent blindness and visual impairment in individuals afflicted by diabetes. The precise and initial identification of DR holds the possible to mitigate vision loss. To support experts in diagnosing DR, a Computer-Aided Analyses prototypical centered on retinal fundus images emerges as a potent instrument. In this domain, certain conventional Machine Learning (ML)-based DR diagnostic models have already been established. Nevertheless, recent strides in Deep Learning (DL) have demonstrated remarkable accomplishments compared to traditional ML algorithms in a variety of applications, rendering it a compelling choice for crafting DR diagnostic models. Fueled by this impetus, this paper introduces an innovative diabetic retinopathy diagnosis model (IDDR) that combines IoT and DL technologies while employing retinal fundus images. The IDDR approach harnesses IoT devices for data collection, followed by the transmission of this data to a cloud server for processing. Subsequently, the retinal fundus imageries undergo preprocessing to eliminate noise then enhance contrast levels. The identification of lesion regions within the fundus image is accomplished through the application of the Ant Colony Algorithm-based region-growing (ACORG) segmentation technique. Furthermore, an effective DR diagnosis is facilitated through a feature extractor based on the densely connected network (DenseNet) and a classifier relying on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Toward fine-tune the parameters of the LSTM method, the Ant Colony Algorithm (ACA) is employed. To assess the enhanced diagnostic outcomes of the IDDR method, a comprehensive series of replications was conducted. A thorough comparative analysis revealed the superior recital of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Thermal Analysis for Enhanced Energy Efficiency in Heat Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Energy efficiency is essential in heat transfer systems to reduce expenses and environmental impact. Traditional thermal analysis methods typically do not adequately address complex, dynamic, and multi-variable scenarios in these systems. This research presents a novel approach for enhancing the energy efficiency of heat transfer systems through the application of machine learning and thermal analysis. The suggested system evaluates temperature gradients, heat flux, and additional thermodynamic parameters in real time through supervised learning techniques. The technology consistently predicts system behavior, identifies inefficiencies, and provides energy-efficient designs by training models on historical and operational data. Gradient Boosting surpassed other machine learning models in accuracy (93.8%), precision (92.5%), recall (93.0%), and F1 score (93.2%). The results indicate significant enhancements in energy efficiency and establish a robust foundation for the design, operation, and optimization of energy systems, yielding advantages for both the environment and the economy.

articleTitle: Hierarchical AI for Optimized 5G RAN Performance: A Distributed Intelligence Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The rapid expansion of 5G networks necessitates advanced optimization techniques to manage the increased complexity and diverse service demands. Hierarchical Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance Radio Access Network (RAN) performance, offering distributed intelligence across cloud, edge, and device levels. This paper explores the integration of hierarchical AI in 5G RAN, emphasizing its potential to optimize resource allocation, reduce latency, and improve Quality of Service (QoS). We propose a framework that leverages AI-driven decision-making at multiple network layers to address the challenges of dynamic traffic management and personalized service delivery. Through comprehensive simulations and case studies, we demonstrate the efficacy of hierarchical AI in achieving real-time optimization, thereby paving the way for more responsive and efficient 5G networks. The findings suggest that hierarchical AI is not only feasible but also essential for the future scalability and adaptability of 5G infrastructure.

articleTitle: Gazelle Optimization Algorithm-Improved SqueezeNet-based Deep Learning Model for Computer Aided Cervical Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer among women worldwide, and early detection plays a crucial role in improving survival rates. The Pap smear test is an efficient screening method that looks at cervical cells to find dysplasia and structural changes in cell shape. This research presents a novel deep-learning method for Computer Aided Cervical Cancer Detection (CACCD), which merges the pre-trained SqueezeNet model with the Gazelle Optimization Algorithm (GOA) to boost detection and classification accuracy. The SqueezeNet model was chosen because it has a compact architecture and can effectively identify essential features and complex patterns from Pap smear test images. The GOA algorithm adjusted model hyperparameters to achieve better performance and accuracy. The performance of this approach was assessed and validated using the Herlev dataset, which serves as a standard benchmark in the domain, and the results showed superior performance compared to other models, including MobileNetV3 and ResNet. The cervical cancer detection method displays strong results according to key performance metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). This study highlights the potential of integrating SqueezeNet with advanced optimization techniques to improve the accuracy and reliability of automated cervical cancer detection.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Inventory Management:Blockchain-Infused GAN Forecasting with ECDH Security Layer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Cloud-based inventory management is one of the most important matters for enterprises nowadays; however, it also includes many challenges, such as data integrity, privacy breaches, and operational inefficiencies. Most existing solutions are not able to provide a secure, scalable, and efficient framework to handle such issues. This paper proposes a blockchain-based hybrid inventory management system empowered by GAN and ECDH techniques. The hybrid blockchain ensures immutable and transparent data storage, while a GAN-based model optimizes inventory forecasting by generating highly accurate demand prediction. ECDH has been incorporated to handle secure key exchange and data encryption in order to safeguard sensitive information during cloud transactions. It will contribute toward enhanced data security, improved forecasting accuracy, and streamlined inventory operations. The proposed advantages are in reducing operational risks, improving privacy, and achieving scalability. This solution will definitely provide an efficient, secure, and modernized framework for inventory management systems in cloud environments.

articleTitle: Identification of Ammunition in Public Environment Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Effective automated security systems are in high demand due to the rise in criminal activity. The deep learning model presented in this work is intended to provide real-time threat identification by identifying and categorizing different kinds of weapons from surveillance data. The model, which was trained on a bespoke dataset that included seven different weapon categories-such as assault rifles, grenades, and pistols-was based on the VGGNet architecture and achieved a 98.4 % accuracy rate. Preprocessing techniques including background removal and rotation modifications were used on the dataset photos to increase robustness. The model demonstrated improved classification accuracy and recall metrics when tested against well-known architectures such as VGG-16, ResNet-50, and ResNet-101. By giving security staff prompt notifications of possible dangers in monitored areas, this technology has useful applications in automated monitoring therefore strengthening preventative security measures, Additional optimization for real-time deployment and integration with intricate security systems will be investigated in future study.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for Detection and Prevention of Attacks in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: VANETs are enabling the advancement of Internet of Vehicles. Network integrity is in great danger from Wormhole Attack (WHA), Black-Hole Attack (BHA), and GrayHole Attack (GHA). To overcome these threats, this research proposes a new security technique called Detection and Prevention of Gray-Hole, Black-Hole, and Wormhole Attacks. In the proposed system, a novel Distributed Detection and Prevention System (DP-GBW), specifically designed for Ad Hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV)-based VANETs, is employed. These attacks may lower the VANETs’ security level, and utilizing this proactive detection and prevention method, ensure a higher level of security. The proposed technique fulfills its intended goal of resisting malicious node attacks while at the same time ensuring that trust values for regular nodes are calculated accurately based on the actual operating environment as supported by simulation experiments. This method enhances the security and reliability of the VANET making the vehicular communication network work together more securely.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Algorithm for Automated Schizophrenia Detection using EEG Signals and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The paper proposes a new hybrid approach for EEG-based automated schizophrenia detection that overcomes the limitations of EEG analysis by human specialists and shallow machine learning (ML) methods, which result in low accuracy and manual feature extraction. The proposed method employs the Wavelet Transform (WT) for efficient feature extraction, followed by a Deep Learning (DL) model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for spatial feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for temporal feature analysis. The synergetic model enhances the accuracy and reliability of diagnosing schizophrenia. The results show that the proposed system's accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity (95.6%, 93.8%, and 96.4%, respectively) clearly surpass the existing one (85.2% and 90.1%). Furthermore, the proposed method reduced false positives (3.2%) and false negatives (4.1%) while achieving the best performance across all parameters and frequency bands, making it an effective tool for clinical early diagnosis applications.

articleTitle: Bagged LSTM Framework for Identifying Suspicious Cryptocurrency Activities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Cryptocurrencies have gained significant popularity; yet, their anonymity and decentralized characteristics render them vulnerable to fraudulent activity. Detecting dubious bitcoin transactions is a formidable endeavor because to the intricacy of the blockchain architecture and the large volume of transactional data. This study introduces an innovative Bagged Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) system aimed at accurately detecting suspicious bitcoin activities. The proposed model utilizes ensemble learning methods by integrating multiple LSTM classifiers to enhance prediction robustness and reduce the likelihood of overfitting. Our method improves anomaly detection in cryptocurrency transactions by consolidating the predictions of several LSTM models, all while preserving computational efficiency. Experimental findings on authentic bitcoin datasets indicate that the Bagged LSTM framework outperforms conventional machine learning (ML) techniques, attaining an accuracy of 92.5%, precision of 91.3%, recall of 90.8%, and an Fl-score of 91.0%. The results underscore the model's efficacy in identifying suspicious behaviors and its capacity to bolster security in cryptocurrency marketplaces, facilitating more dependable detection of fraudulent transactions.

articleTitle: Explainable AI Frameworks for Large Language Models in High-Stakes Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In high-stakes decision-making, such as healthcare diagnostics, financial forecasting, and legal judgments, trust and transparency are key in AI systems. LLMs have indeed proved to be very capable in processing and generating human-like text, making them invaluable tools in these critical sectors. However, the opacity of their decision-making processes poses a significant challenge for accountability and ethical compliance. This paper introduces comprehensive Explainable AI frameworks tailored for LLMs with the goal of improving their interpretability and reliability for high-stakes environments. Using publicly available real-world datasets, we systematically study the effectiveness of various XAI techniques, including attention visualization, feature importance mapping, and counterfactual explanations. Our findings point to the fact that such embedding serves not only to demystify the decision pathways of LLMs but also to bring their operations in line with regulatory standards and stakeholder expectations. This research makes its contribution to responsible LLM deployment in situations where mistakes have significant consequences by closing the gap between sophisticated AI capabilities and the need for transparent decision-making. The proposed XAI frameworks will, in the end, be a starting point for trust, ethics, and wider acceptance of AI-driven solutions in high-stakes domains.

articleTitle: Intelligent Grocery Management System Using IoT for Personalized Shopping and Inventory Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The Intelligent Grocery Management System (IGMS) leverages the power of the Internet of Things (IoT) to revolutionize personalized shopping and inventory management. The proposed system integrates smart sensors, RFID tags, and mobile applications to provide a seamless and efficient shopping experience. The IGMS monitors inventory levels in real-time, automatically generates shopping lists based on consumption patterns, and provides personalized product recommendations using machine learning algorithms. Shoppers can track expiry dates, receive notifications about discounts, and access detailed nutritional insights through a user-friendly mobile app. Additionally, the system enhances inventory management for retailers by predicting demand, reducing waste, and optimizing stock levels. Experimental results demonstrate that the IGMS improves shopping efficiency, reduces household food waste, and enables retailers to streamline operations and enhanced efficacy of the suggested strategy in inventory management, evidenced by its greatest Inventory Turnover Ratio (4.5) and lowest Stockout Rate (5%). This innovative solution aims to transform grocery shopping into a smarter, more sustainable, and personalized experience, catering to the needs of both consumers and businesses.

articleTitle: HealthX: Smart Health Record Management System with Speech Input
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Maintaining personal health records is an essential aspect of modern healthcare, this helps ensure accessibility, efficiency, and solutions that need to be provided. The entire study will enable HealthX, an intelligent health document management system, to manage and store health data using voice commands. The platform engages patients and healthcare providers with the voice-to-text feature-file uploads by how they manage medical records including data entry by voice and usability improvement. Searching through the catalogue of doctors, scheduling an appointment, accessing first-aid information, and securely storing patient history data are the other interesting features. In this case, the system allows digital literacy to be accessed by users with multiple skill levels. The system underwent evaluation by 500 users under different conditions. During this process, the system was found to be 99% accurate in quiet environments, with performance decreasing in noisy settings and strong accents. To address the issue of data security and privacy, HealthX nominates access based on the user roles that are currently defined. Those roles allow patients to view their records, healthcare providers to access only authorized data, and governmental authorities to analyze anonymized data for public health policy development globally. In this way, data safety is guaranteed by accompanying rules and norms by HIPAA, GDPR, and NDHM. The project has its foundation in MongoDB, Express, and Node.js. With the coming of other updates, technologies like speech recognition, wearable device support, and AI-powered analytics for real-time health monitoring, multilingual support, and remote patient care will be the main focus of HealthX, which will thus become an intelligent, secure and patient-centric healthcare solution.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Defect Prediction in Software through SqueezeNet and DenseNet Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In software engineering, forecasting defects is a critical strategy for improving the strength and efficiency of software. This study undertakes a comparative analysis using datasets from NASA to assess the performance of two prominent convolutional neural network models, SqueezeNet and DenseNet, for predicting software Defect. SqueezeNet, known for its parameter efficiency, and DenseNet, celebrated for its feature propagation, were evaluated against various performance indicators such as accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1 score. The study presents a comprehensive examination of the models' performance on the task of binary classification of defective and non-defective software modules. Results indicate that SqueezeNet achieves remarkable precision and accuracy, making it particularly suitable for scenarios requiring the minimization of false positives. In contrast, DenseNet demonstrates robust recall abilities, favoring environments where the detection of all potential defects is critical. The insights gained from this analysis could aid in the strategic selection and implementation of neural network models for software defect prediction.

articleTitle: Efficient Crash Event Handling in VANETs through Authenticity and Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This research introduces a robust protocol for handling crash events within Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs). The protocol focuses on ensuring data authenticity and minimizing network overhead through aggregation techniques. To enforce authenticity, each message related to a crash event is required to be signed by a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) using public key cryptography. Victim and witness vehicles sign information about accident time and location. To optimize network efficiency, the protocol aggregates these signed messages into single packets using signature chaining. Continuous updates are incorporated so that nodes can include additional information as they become aware of it without resetting rebroadcast counters. Simulation results in a highway environment demonstrate that the protocol efficiently disseminates crash information, with selective broadcast and aggregation significantly reducing network traffic. Beyond crash events, the protocol's potential applications encompass hazard notification, traffic management, and dynamic data exchange within VANETs, offering a versatile solution for vehicular communication systems.

articleTitle: Image Classification in Medical Diagnosis for Diabetic Retinopathy-Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: A major contributor to visual impairment, diabetic retinopathy (DR) necessitates early identification for successful treatment. Conventional CNNs, which are employed in DR diagnosis, sometimes have trouble with huge datasets, which results in overfitting and decreased accuracy. To overcome these constraints, a hybrid deep learning model that combines CNN, Inception V3, and VGG19 architectures is suggested. By enhancing the identification of microaneurysms, an early sign of DR, our approach improves feature extraction capabilities. Training and assessment are conducted using the APTOS 2019 dataset, which consists of retinal pictures classified into five groups. Techniques for augmenting data, such as different image reflections, improve resilience and avoid overfitting. When compared to current models, the hybrid model exhibits higher accuracy and provides more trustworthy predictions. The model's efficacy in early DR identification is demonstrated by improved performance measures including accuracy and recall, which may improve patient outcomes by enabling prompt diagnosis and care.

articleTitle: Cluster-Oriented Intelligent Secure Routing Protocol Design for Strengthened Communication in Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) has changed the face of traditional road networks to be smart, connected ecosystems. Vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) are central to this evolution since they provide real-time vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) and vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication that enables data to be transferred between entities for effective management of traffic and enhancement of road safety. There is still much to be covered in the development of VANETs, considering dynamic network topology, security weaknesses, and latency in the data transfer process. Most of the routing protocols currently in use are not efficient and secure, especially when used in high-mobility environments. The need to develop a robust, intelligent, and secure routing protocol that ensures high throughput, low latency, and resilience against malicious attacks is what motivates this research. This study proposes the Cluster-Oriented Intelligent Secure Routing Protocol, GO-SBT-CDN-WaO, which combines cluster-based routing with the Modified Greylag-Goose Optimization (MGGO) algorithm, thereby ensuring optimal path selection. The protocol utilizes a Stacked Bi-Tier Convolutional Deep Network (SBT-CDN) for sophisticated threat detection, which is fine-tuned using the Walrus Optimizer (WaO) to ensure reliable and secure communication. The proposed protocol has achieved outstanding performance metrics: throughput of 99.31%, end-to-end delay less than 1 ms, energy efficiency over 99.74%, with packet delivery ratio (PDR) for 99.5%, and superior scalability across diverse network scenarios. Integration of smart routing, advanced optimisation, and robust security with the GO-SBT-CDN-WaO protocol redefines VANET communication to enable resilient, efficient data exchange in ITS environments.

articleTitle: URBANLITE: A Safe and Secure Transfer of City Data Deploying LIFI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: In contrast to Wi-Fi, Li-Fi (Light Fidelity), a new optical wireless communication technology, employs LED light to convey data more quickly and adaptable. Since light is present practically everywhere, communication may be done with ease. Li-Fi offers greater speed, improved security, and immunity to electromagnetic interference in contrast to Wi-Fi, which uses radio waves to transport data. This makes it the perfect choice for smart homes, smart cities, and industrial automation. By utilising the current LED infrastructure, Li-Fi-based automation makes it possible for devices, sensors, and controllers to communicate in real time. It guarantees safe, fast, and energy-efficient data communication, lowering energy usage and enhancing control over equipment such as traffic signals, lighting, and industrial systems. Li-Fi offers enormous potential in sectors like manufacturing, healthcare, and smart cities. But issues like infrastructural constraints and line-of-sight requirements still need to be resolved. Li-Fi presents a bright future for safe, effective, and scalable automation systems in spite of these obstacles.

articleTitle: A Platform-agnostic Solution for a Pluggable and Customizable Approach to Zero Trust Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Every day, cybercriminals discover new methods to illegally access devices and networks. Cybercriminals not only compromise digital privacy, but also pose a risk to financial stability and reputation. These days, traditional security measures to safeguard the organization have proven insufficient. Consequently, the concept of zero trust was introduced. It is a new approach to cybersecurity that involves never trusting any device or entity without verifying them. Since its inception, various architectures were proposed and came into action. However, there is a lack of zero trust architecture that is customizable, deployable with ease, and is platform independent. In order to address this issue, we propose a platform-agnostic, pluggable, and customizable zero trust architecture that is easy to deploy and requires less migration downtime. It gives organizations the freedom to customize the users, resources, policies, access control, etc., supporting less migration downtime and the ability for novice users to maintain it. This research proposes the high-level step-by-step workflow of the architecture as well as various technical details needed at each step. This architecture can be extended as a base for various other future research projects utilizing zero trust security in different domains.

articleTitle: Advancing the Metaverse: The Convergence of Digital Twins, AI, and Emerging Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) has led to technical breakthroughs in various fields. AI has now improved services in smart cities, healthcare, agriculture, and education. It would not have been possible to achieve these technological achievements without quick, safe, and reliable communication channels. For realistic services, the conventional processing, interaction, and storage methods available cannot maintain and provide the elevated level of flexibility and user experience desired. Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) technology is used to create the metaverse, an immersive three-dimensional (3D) virtual world that combines reality and fantasy. Such an ecosystem is still in the early stages of development and will need much research to reach its full potential. Some of the most important issues needed to materialize the metaverse are covered in this paper. To sustain continuous end-to-end metaverse services, a framework combining digital twins (DT) with other cutting-edge technologies, including blockchain, artificial intelligence, and sixth-generation (6G) communication networks is needed. All the criteria required for an integrated DT-enabled metaverse framework are also described in this paper in detail, which offers a complete outlook on these developing fields.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-XAI Model for Predicting Student Academic Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This study presents a combined method that improves the ability to predict and understand outcomes by merging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). The approach can pinpoint effective predictors by uncovering intricate patterns from behavioural data using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). XAI techniques ensure that instructors can gain valuable insights by clearly outlining the role of each component. The model greatly surpasses traditional methods, reaching an impressive 96% accuracy rate and a micro-average AUC score of 0.86 and achieved 95% precision, 95.5% F1-score, and a perfect Cohen's Kappa of 1.0, showcasing exceptional reliability. The results show how well the proposed system can generate interpretive data and its reliability in predicting grades. The hybrid CNN-XAI model empowers educators by enhancing their decision-making freedom, boosting prediction abilities, and aligning with contemporary teaching methods.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Anomaly Detection in Software-Defined Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The advent of Software-Defined Networks (SDN) introduces centralized management, enabling scalability to support a significantly larger number of devices than traditional networks. However, this scalability generates extensive monitoring data, necessitating advanced analysis techniques. This research focuses on utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the SDN paradigm to enhance anomaly detection. A systematic literature review identified current challenges and opportunities in this domain. Based on these insights, a reference architecture was developed, integrating advanced features such as dynamic sliding windows for training optimization, a standardized ubiquitous data model, and separation of concerns (SoC) leveraging industry-standard frameworks like eTOM and SID. The architecture emphasizes interpretability through explainable AI (XAI), scalability via microservices, and resilience with a distributed SDN controller. Adversarial sample generation was incorporated to strengthen anomaly detection models. A proof of concept validated the architecture's feasibility, demonstrating successful anomaly detection and remediation across varying business scenarios. This study highlights the adaptability of AI models for specific anomaly types and underscores the potential of this architecture in automating large-scale network management, enhancing security, and increasing resilience.

articleTitle: Building Resilient Web Applications with Continuous Deployment and Microservices: Crafting Scalable and Secure Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Creating sustainable web applications with agile deployment and breaking down apps into microservices for scalability and security. This study explores the implementation of microservice architecture in the context of building resilient web applications with continuous deployment, focusing on crafting scalable and secure architectures. The research examines the impact of microservices on the scalability, performance, and security of a loan payment plan application offered as a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) model. The application is composed of two primary services: payment plan generation (S1) and payment plan retrieval (S2). Since the study looks at monolithic architecture and micro-service architecture on AWS, the study provides an understanding of the performance gain, cost of infrastructure, and resource optimization in both models. The outcome proves that microservice delivers better scalability, flexibility, and the ability to scale the particular service, which plays a significant role in web application's high availability and performance. Furthermore, it makes continuous deployment possible and simpler, making it possible for organizations to update faster. The study concluded that microservices gave more long-term flexibility and scalability and were suitable for applications requiring independent service scaling.

articleTitle: Efficient Nearest Neighbor Search in Large-Scale Text Data Using Optimized Locality Sensitive Hashing in Distributed Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Efficient nearest neighbor search is crucial for applications such as web search, mobile browsing, and Natural Language Processing (NLP), where rapid text retrieval from vast datasets is required. As data scales, traditional brute- force approaches become computationally expensive, necessitating optimized methods. This work introduces an enhanced Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) framework tailored for distributed computing environments, leveraging Hadoop for large-scale processing. By incorporating optimized LSH variants, our approach improves efficiency while maintaining high recall rates. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method surpasses conventional LSH implementations in retrieval accuracy while ensuring computational scalability, making it suitable for real-world applications requiring rapid text similarity assessments.

articleTitle: Learning Techniques for Personalized Oxygen Therapy in Pulmonary Rehabilitation Using Cloud Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: Personalized oxygen treatment is essential to maximize pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) for individuals with long-term respiratory disorders. This research offers a unique method to improve oxygen treatment customization by integrating advanced deep learning techniques within cloud-based architecture, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. To allow for personalized oxygen treatment changes, the proposed solution combines LSTM networks with cloud computing capabilities to collect and evaluate large amounts of health data and indicators from real-time monitoring. With LSTM networks, complicated temporal patterns in patient data may be captured and learned, leading to more accurate treatment predictions and changes. Treatment plans are continuously modified depending on individual patient demands and changing health situations; the system provides scalable and adaptable solutions for ongoing therapy optimization using cloud infrastructure. A battery of tests contrasting the device with conventional oxygen treatment techniques proves its efficacy. The results significantly improve the accuracy of predictions, treatment classification, and patient adherence. An effective, scalable, and patient-centered solution for controlling oxygen treatment in varied clinical settings may be achieved by merging deep learning with cloud technology; our study highlights the revolutionary potential of this combination in pulmonary rehabilitation. LSTM networks combined with cloud computing provide a huge step forward in individualized medicine, which may contribute to better results for chronic respiratory disease patients.

articleTitle: Data Redundancy Optimization in HDFS via Machine Learning Clustering Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: HDFS is the Hadoop Distributed File System, a critical part of big data storage, but processes suffer from lots of inefficiency due to duplicated data. In this paper, we propose to use machine learning as the core foundation of clustering algorithms such as K-means, DBSCAN, and hierarchical clustering to optimize data redundancy in HDFS. This entire methodology involves preprocessing raw data, feature extraction, and clustering similar data blocks together to reduce redundancy. We analyze key evaluation metrics: Get Storage Savings, Retrieval Time Improvement, and Scalability. K-means resulted in a 30<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\% }}$</tex> improvement in retrieval times while achieving the highest storage reduction of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%$25{{\% }}$</tex>. But DBSCAN handled noisy data well and hierarchical clustering provided granular relationships at the cost of high computational cost. We have demonstrated scalability and real-world practical application of this approach in such large-scale data environments with which we can perform sustainable data storage cost optimization as well as improved data retrieval performance in distributed systems. Future work will also examine dynamic clustering techniques as well as hybrid models that can improve system performance and adaptability even further.

articleTitle: Enhancing 5G RAN Agility: Cloud-Native Architectures For Rapid Deployment And Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of telecommunications technology and the rise of 5G Radio Access Network (RAN) demand an agile and adaptive framework capable of addressing the increasing need for swift deployment and efficient maintenance. Traditional RAN architectures, often constrained by rigid hardware-based implementations, fall short of meeting these modern requirements. This paper explores the transformative potential of integrating cloud-native architectures within the 5G RAN ecosystem to significantly enhance its flexibility, scalability, and operational efficiency. We propose a comprehensive cloud-native 5G RAN architecture that leverages key cloud-native principles such as containerization, microservices, and orchestration technologies to support faster deployment, automated maintenance, and dynamic scaling of network resources. By encapsulating network functions into lightweight, portable containers, and decomposing them into independent microservices, our architecture ensures modularity and facilitates continuous integration and deployment processes. The utilization of orchestration tools like Kubernetes automates the management and operation of these containerized applications, ensuring high availability and scalability. Through detailed analysis and illustrative use cases, we demonstrate how cloud-native 5G RAN can accommodate the evolving demands of next-generation telecommunications, including the ability to dynamically allocate and scale resources in real-time. Our findings highlight the potential of this novel approach to simplify network deployment and maintenance while improving the overall agility and resilience of 5G RAN infrastructures. As the telecommunications industry progresses towards 6G and beyond, the insights from this research offer a foundational blueprint for future network evolution.

articleTitle: Dual Source Renewable Charger For Electrical Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: The study introduces a novel Dual Source Renewable Charger for electric vehicles (EVs) that uses wind and solar energy to improve charging dependability and efficiency. Under ideal circumstances, the system's overall energy efficiency ranges from 85 to 90%, which is a 15–20% increase over single-source renewable charging systems. A typical EV battery can be charged in 6–8 hours thanks to its 1.5–2.5 kW combined power output under average sun irradiation (800 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and wind speeds (5–7 m/s). The system includes a hybrid renewable energy model with solar panels and a vertical-axis wind turbine, as well as an intelligent power management unit that dynamically prioritizes energy sources according to availability and environmental circumstances. The design incorporates a 10 kWh energy storage system to mitigate energy intermittency, guaranteeing continuous charging for 4–6 hours during periods of low renewable energy supply. By restricting charge/discharge cycles to 95% depth of discharge (DoD), the adaptive charging approach incorporates a bidirectional DC-DC converter, prolonging battery longevity by 20–25% in comparison to traditional methods. The charger also lowers operating expenses and carbon impact by reducing grid reliance by 60–70% during periods of peak renewable energy output. The system's Internet of Things (IoT) features allow for real-time monitoring and optimization, improve user comfort and grid compatibility, and reduce energy losses by 5–10% through adaptive power management and predictive maintenance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Music Discovery: A Real-Time Recommendation System using Sentiment Analysis and Emotional Matching with Spotify Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Advanced Computing Technologies (ICoACT)
abstract: This paper presents an emotion-based music recommendation system that utilizes sentiment analysis and emotion recognition to provide personalized music suggestions based on the user's emotional state. The system processes both text and audio inputs, using emotion detection models such as Hugging Face's aiknowyou/it-emotion-analyzer and pysentimiento for sentiment classification. Music recommendations are made by mapping the detected emotions to relevant music genres with the help of the Spotify API. The system was evaluated based on emotion detection accuracy and the relevance of the music recommendations. Results showed high accuracy in emotion detection from text inputs, with text achieving an accuracy rate of 92.5% for joy and 94.3% for sadness, while audio inputs demonstrated slightly lower accuracy, with a maximum of 91.0% for sadness. The music recommendation system achieved an 88.5% user satisfaction rate, with over 90% accuracy in artist-specific matching. Despite the challenges in mapping emotions like fear and surprise to appropriate genres, the system provided fast real-time recommendations with an average response time of 350 milliseconds.
